1.1: In the beginning of God's preparing the heavens and the earth--
1.2: the earth has existed waste and void, and darkness is on the face of the deep, and the Spirit of God fluttering on the face of the waters,
1.3: and God says, `Let light be;' and light is.
1.4: And God sees the light that it is good, and God separates between the light and the darkness,
1.5: and God calls to the light `Day,' and to the darkness He has called `Night;' and there is an evening, and there is a morning--day one.
1.6: And God says, `Let an expanse be in the midst of the waters, and let it be separating between waters and waters.'
1.7: And God makes the expanse, and it separates between the waters which are under the expanse, and the waters which are above the expanse: and it is so.
1.8: And God calls to the expanse `Heavens;' and there is an evening, and there is a morning--day second.
1.9: And God says, `Let the waters under the heavens be collected to one place, and let the dry land be seen:' and it is so.
1.10: And God calls to the dry land `Earth,' and to the collection of the waters He has called `Seas;' and God sees that it is good.
1.11: And God says, `Let the earth yield tender grass, herb sowing seed, fruit-tree (whose seed is in itself) making fruit after its kind, on the earth:' and it is so.
1.12: And the earth brings forth tender grass, herb sowing seed after its kind, and tree making fruit (whose seed is in itself) after its kind; and God sees that it is good;
1.13: and there is an evening, and there is a morning--day third.
1.14: And God says, `Let luminaries be in the expanse of the heavens, to make a separation between the day and the night, then they have been for signs, and for seasons, and for days and years,
1.15: and they have been for luminaries in the expanse of the heavens to give light upon the earth:' and it is so.
1.16: And God makes the two great luminaries, the great luminary for the rule of the day, and the small luminary--and the stars--for the rule of the night;
1.17: and God gives them in the expanse of the heavens to give light upon the earth,
1.18: and to rule over day and over night, and to make a separation between the light and the darkness; and God sees that it is good;
1.19: and there is an evening, and there is a morning--day fourth.
1.20: And God says, `Let the waters teem with the teeming living creature, and fowl let fly on the earth on the face of the expanse of the heavens.'
1.21: And God prepares the great monsters, and every living creature that is creeping, which the waters have teemed with, after their kind, and every fowl with wing, after its kind, and God sees that it is good.
1.22: And God blesses them, saying, `Be fruitful, and multiply, and fill the waters in the seas, and the fowl let multiply in the earth:'
1.23: and there is an evening, and there is a morning--day fifth.
1.24: And God says, `Let the earth bring forth the living creature after its kind, cattle and creeping thing, and beast of the earth after its kind:' and it is so.
1.25: And God makes the beast of the earth after its kind, and the cattle after their kind, and every creeping thing of the ground after its kind, and God sees that it is good.
1.26: And God says, `Let Us make man in Our image, according to Our likeness, and let them rule over fish of the sea, and over fowl of the heavens, and over cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that is creeping on the earth.'
1.27: And God prepares the man in His image; in the image of God He prepared him, a male and a female He prepared them.
1.28: And God blesses them, and God says to them, `Be fruitful, and multiply, and fill the earth, and subdue it, and rule over fish of the sea, and over fowl of the heavens, and over every living thing that is creeping upon the earth.'
1.29: And God says, `Indeed, I have given to you every herb sowing seed, which is upon the face of all the earth, and every tree in which is the fruit of a tree sowing seed, to you it is for food;
1.30: and to every beast of the earth, and to every fowl of the heavens, and to every creeping thing on the earth, in which is breath of life, every green herb is for food:' and it is so.
1.31: And God sees all that He has done, and indeed, very good; and there is an evening, and there is a morning--day the sixth.

2.1: And the heavens and the earth are completed, and all their host;
2.2: and God completes by the seventh day His work which He has made, and ceases by the seventh day from all His work which He has made.
2.3: And God blesses the seventh day, and sanctifies it, for in it He has ceased from all His work which God had prepared for making.
2.4: These are births of the heavens and of the earth in their being prepared, in the day of Jehovah God's making earth and heavens;
2.5: and no shrub of the field is yet in the earth, and no herb of the field yet sprouts, for Jehovah God has not rained upon the earth, and a man there is not to serve the ground,
2.6: and a mist goes up from the earth, and has watered the whole face of the ground.
2.7: And Jehovah God forms the man--dust from the ground, and breathes into his nostrils breath of life, and the man becomes a living creature.
2.8: And Jehovah God plants a garden in Eden, at the east, and He sets there the man whom He has formed;
2.9: and Jehovah God causes to sprout from the ground every tree desirable for appearance, and good for food, and the tree of life in the midst of the garden, and the tree of knowledge of good and evil.
2.10: And a river is going out from Eden to water the garden, and from from there it is parted, and has become four chief rivers;
2.11: the name of the one is Pison, it is that which is surrounding the whole land of the Havilah where the gold is,
2.12: and the gold of that land is good, there is the bdolach and the shoham stone;
2.13: and the name of the second river is Gibon, it is that which is surrounding the whole land of Cush;
2.14: and the name of the third river is Hiddekel, it is that which is going east of Asshur; and the fourth river is Phrat.
2.15: And Jehovah God takes the man, and causes him to rest in the garden of Eden, to serve it, and to keep it.
2.16: And Jehovah God lays a charge on the man, saying, `Of every tree of the garden eating you do eat;
2.17: and of the tree of knowledge of good and evil, you do not eat of it, for in the day of your eating of it--dying you do die.'
2.18: And Jehovah God says, `Not good for the man to be alone, I do make to him an helper--as his counterpart.'
2.19: And Jehovah God forms from the ground every beast of the field, and every fowl of the heavens, and brings in to the man, to see what he does call it; and whatever the man calls a living creature, that is its name.
2.20: And the man calls names to all the cattle, and to fowl of the heavens, and to every beast of the field; and to man has not been found an helper--as his counterpart.
2.21: And Jehovah God causes a deep sleep to fall upon the man, and he sleeps, and He takes one of his ribs, and closes up flesh in its stead.
2.22: And Jehovah God builds up the rib which He has taken out of the man into a woman, and brings her in to the man;
2.23: and the man says, `This is the proper step! bone of my bone, and flesh of my flesh!' for this it is called Woman, for from a man has this been taken;
2.24: therefore does a man leave his father and his mother, and has cleaved to his wife, and they have become one flesh.
2.25: And they are both of them naked, the man and his wife, and they are not ashamed of themselves.

3.1: And the serpent has been subtile above every beast of the field which Jehovah God has made, and he says to the woman, `Is it true that God has said, You do not eat of every tree of the garden?'
3.2: And the woman says to the serpent, `Of the fruit of the trees of the garden we do eat,
3.3: and of the fruit of the tree which is in the midst of the garden God has said, You do not eat of it, nor touch it, lest you die.'
3.4: And the serpent says to the woman, `Dying, you do not die,
3.5: for God does know that in the day of your eating of it--your eyes have been opened, and you have been as God, knowing good and evil.'
3.6: And the woman sees that the tree is good for food, and that it is pleasant to the eyes, and the tree is desirable to make one wise, and she takes of its fruit and eats, and gives also to her husband with her, and he does eat;
3.7: and the eyes of them both are opened, and they know that they are naked, and they sew fig-leaves, and make to themselves girdles.
3.8: And they hear the sound of Jehovah God walking up and down in the garden at the breeze of the day, and the man and his wife hide themselves from the face of Jehovah God in the midst of the trees of the garden.
3.9: And Jehovah God calls to the man, and says to him, `Where are you?'
3.10: and he says, `Your sound I have heard in the garden, and I am afraid, for I am naked, and I hide myself.'
3.11: And He says, `Who has declared to you that you are naked? of the tree of which I have commanded you not to eat, have you eaten?'
3.12: and the man says, `The woman whom You did place with me--she has given to me of the tree--and I do eat.'
3.13: And Jehovah God says to the woman, `What is this you have done?' and the woman says, `The serpent has caused me to forget--and I do eat.'
3.14: And Jehovah God says to the serpent, `Because you have done this, cursed are you above all the cattle, and above every beast of the field: on your belly do you go, and dust you do eat, all days of your life;
3.15: and enmity I put between you and the woman, and between your seed and her seed; he does bruise you--the head, and you do bruise him--the heel.'
3.16: To the woman He said, `Multiplying I multiply your sorrow and your conception, in sorrow do you bear children, and toward your husband is your desire, and he does rule over you.'
3.17: And to the man He said, `Because you have hearkened to the voice of your wife, and do eat of the tree concerning which I have charged you, saying, You do not eat of it, cursed is the ground on your account; in sorrow you do eat of it all days of your life,
3.18: and thorn and bramble it does bring forth to you, and you have eaten the herb of the field;
3.19: by the sweat of your face you do eat bread till your return to the ground, for out of it have you been taken, for dust you are, and to dust you turn back.'
3.20: And the man calls his wife's name Eve: for she has been mother of all living.
3.21: And Jehovah God does make to the man and to his wife coats of skin, and does clothe them.
3.22: And Jehovah God says, `Indeed, the man was as one of Us, as to the knowledge of good and evil; and now, lest he send forth his hand, and have taken also of the tree of life, and eaten, and lived to the age,' --
3.23: Jehovah God sends him forth from the garden of Eden to serve the ground from which he has been taken;
3.24: yes, he casts out the man, and causes to dwell at the east of the garden of Eden the cherubs and the flame of the sword which is turning itself round to guard the way of the tree of life.

4.1: And the man knew Eve his wife, and she conceives and bears Cain, and says, `I have gotten a man by Jehovah;'
4.2: and she adds to bear his brother, even Abel. And Abel is feeding a flock, and Cain has been servant of the ground.
4.3: And it comes to pass at the end of days that Cain brings from the fruit of the ground a present to Jehovah;
4.4: and Abel, he has brought, he also, from the female firstlings of his flock, even from their fat ones; and Jehovah looks to Abel and to his present,
4.5: and to Cain and to his present He has not looked; and it is very displeasing to Cain, and his countenance is fallen.
4.6: And Jehovah says to Cain, `Why have you displeasure? and why has your countenance fallen?
4.7: Is there not, if you do well, acceptance? and if you do not well, at the opening a sin-offering is crouching, and to you its desire, and you rule over it.'
4.8: And Cain says to Abel his brother, `Let us go into the field;' and it comes to pass in their being in the field, that Cain rises up against Abel his brother, and slays him.
4.9: And Jehovah says to Cain, `Where is Abel your brother?' and he says, `I have not known; my brother's keeper--I?'
4.10: And He says, `What have you done? the voice of your brother's blood is crying to Me from the ground;
4.11: and now, cursed are you from the ground, which has opened her mouth to receive the blood of your brother from your hand;
4.12: when you till the ground, it does not add to give its strength to you--a wanderer, even a trembling one, you are in the earth.'
4.13: And Cain says to Jehovah, `Greater is my punishment than to be borne;
4.14: indeed, You have driven me to-day from off the face of the ground, and from Your face I am hid; and I have been a wanderer, even a trembling one, in the earth, and it has been--every one finding me does slay me.'
4.15: And Jehovah says to him, `Therefore--of any slayer of Cain sevenfold it is required;' and Jehovah sets to Cain a token that none finding him does slay him.
4.16: And Cain goes out from before Jehovah, and dwells in the land, moving about east of Eden;
4.17: and Cain knows his wife, and she conceives, and bears Enoch; and he is building a city, and he calls the name of the city, according to the name of his son--Enoch.
4.18: And born to Enoch is Irad; and Irad has begotten Mehujael; and Mehujael has begotten Methusael; and Methusael has begotten Lamech.
4.19: And Lamech takes to himself two wives, the name of the one Adah, and the name of the second Zillah.
4.20: And Adah bears Jabal, he has been father of those inhabiting tents and purchased possessions;
4.21: and the name of his brother is Jubal, he has been father of every one handling harp and organ.
4.22: And Zillah she also bare Tubal-Cain, an instructor of every artificer in brass and iron; and a sister of Tubal-Cain is Naamah.
4.23: And Lamech says to his wives: --`Adah and Zillah, hear my voice; Wives of Lamech, give ear to my saying: For a man I have slain for my wound, Even a young man for my hurt;
4.24: For sevenfold is required for Cain, And for Lamech seventy and sevenfold.'
4.25: And Adam again knows his wife, and she bears a son, and calls his name Seth, `for God has appointed for me another seed instead of Abel:' for Cain had slain him.
4.26: And to Seth, to him also a son has been born, and he calls his name Enos; then a beginning was made of preaching in the name of Jehovah.

5.1: This is an account of the births of Adam: In the day of God's preparing man, in the likeness of God He has made him;
5.2: a male and a female He has prepared them, and He blesses them, and calls their name Man, in the day of their being prepared.
5.3: And Adam lives an hundred and thirty years, and begets a son in his likeness, according to his image, and calls his name Seth.
5.4: And the days of Adam after his begetting Seth are eight hundred years, and he begets sons and daughters.
5.5: And all the days of Adam which he lived are nine hundred and thirty years, and he dies.
5.6: And Seth lives an hundred and five years, and begets Enos.
5.7: And Seth lives after his begetting Enos eight hundred and seven years, and begets sons and daughters.
5.8: And all the days of Seth are nine hundred and twelve years, and he dies.
5.9: And Enos lives ninety years, and begets Cainan.
5.10: And Enos lives after his begetting Cainan eight hundred and fifteen years, and begets sons and daughters.
5.11: And all the days of Enos are nine hundred and five years, and he dies.
5.12: And Cainan lives seventy years, and begets Mahalaleel.
5.13: And Cainan lives after his begetting Mahalaleel eight hundred and forty years, and begets sons and daughters.
5.14: And all the days of Cainan are nine hundred and ten years, and he dies.
5.15: And Mahalaleel lives five and sixty years, and begets Jared.
5.16: And Mahalaleel lives after his begetting Jared eight hundred and thirty years, and begets sons and daughters.
5.17: And all the days of Mahalaleel are eight hundred and ninety and five years, and he dies.
5.18: And Jared lives an hundred and sixty and two years, and begets Enoch.
5.19: And Jared lives after his begetting Enoch eight hundred years, and begets sons and daughters.
5.20: And all the days of Jared are nine hundred and sixty and two years, and he dies.
5.21: And Enoch lives five and sixty years, and begets Methuselah.
5.22: And Enoch walks habitually with God after his begetting Methuselah three hundred years, and begets sons and daughters.
5.23: And all the days of Enoch are three hundred and sixty and five years.
5.24: And Enoch walks habitually with God, and he is not, for God has taken him.
5.25: And Methuselah lives an hundred and eighty and seven years, and begets Lamech.
5.26: And Methuselah lives after his begetting Lamech seven hundred and eighty and two years, and begets sons and daughters.
5.27: And all the days of Methuselah are nine hundred and sixty and nine years, and he dies.
5.28: And Lamech lives an hundred and eighty and two years, and begets a son,
5.29: and calls his name Noah, saying, `This one does comfort us concerning our work, and concerning the labour of our hands, because of the ground which Jehovah has cursed.'
5.30: And Lamech lives after his begetting Noah five hundred and ninety and five years, and begets sons and daughters.
5.31: And all the days of Lamech are seven hundred and seventy and seven years, and he dies.
5.32: And Noah is a son of five hundred years, and Noah begets Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

6.1: And it comes to pass that mankind have begun to multiply on the face of the ground, and daughters have been born to them,
6.2: and sons of God see the daughters of men that they are fair, and they take to themselves women of all whom they have chosen.
6.3: And Jehovah says, `My Spirit does not strive in man--to the age; in their erring they are flesh:' and his days have been an hundred and twenty years.
6.4: The fallen ones were in the earth in those days, and even afterwards when sons of God come in to daughters of men, and they have borne to them--they are the heroes, who, from of old, are the men of name.
6.5: And Jehovah sees that abundant is the wickedness of man in the earth, and every imagination of the thoughts of his heart only evil all the day;
6.6: and Jehovah repents that He has made man in the earth, and He grieves Himself--to His heart.
6.7: And Jehovah says, `I wipe away man whom I have prepared from off the face of the ground, from man to beast, to creeping thing, and to fowl of the heavens, for I have repented that I have made them.'
6.8: And Noah found grace in the eyes of Jehovah.
6.9: These are births of Noah: Noah is a righteous man; perfect he has been among his generations; with God has Noah walked habitually.
6.10: And Noah begets three sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
6.11: And the earth is corrupt before God, and the earth is filled with violence.
6.12: And God sees the earth, and indeed, it has been corrupted, for all flesh has corrupted its way on the earth.
6.13: And God said to Noah, `An end of all flesh has come before Me, for the earth has been full of violence from their presence; and indeed, I am destroying them with the earth.
6.14: `Make for yourself an ark of gopher-wood; rooms do you make with the ark, and you have covered it within and without with cypress;
6.15: and this is that which you do with it: three hundred cubits is the length of the ark, fifty cubits its breadth, and thirty cubits its height;
6.16: a window do you make for the ark, and to a cubit you do restrain it from above; and the opening of the ark you do put in its side, --lower, second, and third stories do you make it.
6.17: `And I, indeed, I am bringing in the deluge of waters on the earth to destroy all flesh, in which is a living spirit, from under the heavens; all that is in the earth does expire.
6.18: `And I have established My covenant with you, and you have come in to the ark, you, and your sons, and your wife, and your son's wives with you;
6.19: and of all that lives, of all flesh, two of every sort you do bring in to the ark, to keep alive with you; male and female are they.
6.20: Of the fowl after its kind, and of the cattle after their kind, of every creeping thing of the ground after its kind, two of every sort they come in to you, to keep alive.
6.21: `And you, take to yourself of all food that is eaten; and you have gathered to yourself, and it has been to you and to them for food.'
6.22: And Noah does according to all that God has commanded him; so has he done.

7.1: And Jehovah says to Noah, `Come in, you and all your house, to the ark, for you I have seen righteous before Me in this generation;
7.2: of all the clean beasts you do take to you seven pairs, a male and its female; and of the beasts which are not clean two, a male and its female;
7.3: also, of fowl of the heavens seven pairs, a male and a female, to keep alive seed on the face of all the earth;
7.4: for after other seven days I am sending rain on the earth forty days and forty nights, and have wiped away all the substance that I have made from off the face of the ground.'
7.5: And Noah does according to all that Jehovah has commanded him:
7.6: and Noah is a son of six hundred years, and the deluge of waters has been upon the earth.
7.7: And Noah goes in, and his sons, and his wife, and his sons' wives with him, to the ark, from the presence of the waters of the deluge;
7.8: of the clean beasts and of the beasts that are not clean, and of the fowl, and of every thing that is creeping upon the ground,
7.9: two by two they have come in to Noah, to the ark, a male and a female, as God has commanded Noah.
7.10: And it comes to pass, after the seventh of the days, that waters of the deluge have been on the earth.
7.11: In the six hundredth year of the life of Noah, in the second month, in the seventeenth day of the month, in this day have been broken up all fountains of the great deep, and the net-work of the heavens has been opened,
7.12: and the shower is on the earth forty days and forty nights.
7.13: In this self-same day went in Noah, and Shem, and Ham, and Japheth, sons of Noah, and Noah's wife and the three wives of his sons with them, to the ark;
7.14: they, and every living creature after its kind, and every beast after its kind, and every creeping thing that is creeping on the earth after its kind, and every fowl after its kind, every bird--every wing.
7.15: And they come in to Noah, to the ark, two by two of all the flesh in which is a living spirit;
7.16: and they that are coming in, male and female of all flesh, have come in as God has commanded him, and Jehovah does close it for him.
7.17: And the deluge is forty days on the earth, and the waters multiply, and lift up the ark, and it is raised up from off the earth;
7.18: and the waters are mighty, and multiply exceedingly upon the earth; and the ark goes on the face of the waters.
7.19: And the waters have been very very mighty on the earth, and covered are all the high mountains which are under the whole heavens;
7.20: fifteen cubits upwards have the waters become mighty, and the mountains are covered;
7.21: and expire does all flesh that is moving on the earth, among fowl, and among cattle, and among beasts, and among all the teeming things which are teeming on the earth, and all mankind;
7.22: all in whose nostrils is breath of a living spirit--of all that is in the dry land--have died.
7.23: And wiped away is all the substance that is on the face of the ground, from man to beast, to creeping thing, and to fowl of the heavens; yes, they are wiped away from the earth, and only Noah is left, and those who are with him in the ark;
7.24: and the waters are mighty on the earth a hundred and fifty days.

8.1: And God remembers Noah, and every living thing, and all the cattle which are with him in the ark, and God causes a wind to pass over the earth, and the waters subside,
8.2: and closed are the fountains of the deep and the net-work of the heavens, and restrained is the shower from the heavens.
8.3: And turn back do the waters from off the earth, going on and returning; and the waters are lacking at the end of a hundred and fifty days.
8.4: And the ark rests, in the seventh month, in the seventeenth day of the month, on mountains of Ararat;
8.5: and the waters have been going and becoming lacking till the tenth month; in the tenth month, on the first of the month, appeared the heads of the mountains.
8.6: And it comes to pass, at the end of forty days, that Noah opens the window of the ark which he made,
8.7: and he sends forth the raven, and it goes out, going out and turning back till the drying of the waters from off the earth.
8.8: And he sends forth the dove from him to see whether the waters have been lightened from off the face of the ground,
8.9: and the dove has not found rest for the sole of her foot, and she turns back to him, to the ark, for waters are on the face of all the earth, and he puts out his hand, and takes her, and brings her in to him, to the ark.
8.10: And he stays yet other seven days, and adds to send forth the dove from the ark;
8.11: and the dove comes in to him at even-time, and indeed, an olive leaf torn off in her mouth; and Noah knows that the waters have been lightened from off the earth.
8.12: And he stays yet other seven days, and sends forth the dove, and it added not to turn back to him any more.
8.13: And it comes to pass in the six hundredth and first year, in the first month, in the first of the month, the waters have been dried from off the earth; and Noah turns aside the covering of the ark, and looks, and indeed, the face of the ground has been dried.
8.14: And in the second month, in the seven and twentieth day of the month, the earth has become dry.
8.15: And God speaks to Noah, saying, `Go out from the ark, you, and your wife, and your sons, and your sons' wives with you;
8.16: every living thing that is with you, of all flesh, among fowl, and among cattle, and among every creeping thing which is creeping on the earth, bring out with you;
8.17: and they have teemed in the earth, and been fruitful, and have multiplied on the earth.'
8.18: And Noah goes out, and his sons, and his wife, and his sons' wives with him;
8.19: every beast, every creeping thing, and every fowl; every creeping thing on the earth, after their families, have gone out from the ark.
8.20: And Noah builds an altar to Jehovah, and takes of every clean beast, and of every clean fowl, and causes burnt-offerings to ascend on the altar;
8.21: and Jehovah smells the sweet fragrance, and Jehovah says to His heart, `I continue not to disesteem any more the ground because of man, though the imagination of the heart of man is evil from his youth; and I continue not to smite any more all living, as I have done;
8.22: during all days of the earth, seed-time and harvest, and cold and heat, and summer and winter, and day and night, do not cease.'

9.1: And God blesses Noah, and his sons, and says to them, `Be fruitful, and multiply, and fill the earth;
9.2: and your fear and your dread is on every beast of the earth, and on every fowl of the heavens, on all that creeps on the ground, and on all fishes of the sea--into your hand they have been given.
9.3: Every creeping thing that is alive, to you it is for food; as the green herb I have given to you the whole;
9.4: only flesh in its life--its blood--you do not eat.
9.5: `And only your blood for your lives do I require; from the hand of every living thing I require it, and from the hand of man, from the hand of every man's brother I require the life of man;
9.6: whoever sheds man's blood, by man is his blood shed: for in the image of God has He made man.
9.7: And you, be fruitful and multiply, teem in the earth, and multiply in it.'
9.8: And God speaks to Noah, and to his sons with him, saying,
9.9: `And I, indeed, I am establishing My covenant with you, and with your seed after you,
9.10: and with every living creature which is with you, among fowl, among cattle, and among every beast of the earth with you, from all who are going out of the ark--to every beast of the earth.
9.11: And I have established My covenant with you, and all flesh is not any more cut off by waters of a deluge, and there is not any more a deluge to destroy the earth.'
9.12: And God says, `This is a token of the covenant which I am giving between Me and you, and every living creature that is with you, to generations age-during;
9.13: My bow I have given in the cloud, and it has been for a token of a covenant between Me and the earth;
9.14: and it has come to pass (in My sending a cloud over the earth) that the bow has been seen in the cloud,
9.15: and I have remembered My covenant which is between Me and you, and every living creature among all flesh, and the waters become no more a deluge to destroy all flesh;
9.16: and the bow has been in the cloud, and I have seen it--to remember the covenant age-during between God and every living creature among all flesh which is on the earth.'
9.17: And God says to Noah, `This is a token of the covenant which I have established between Me and all flesh that is upon the earth.'
9.18: And the sons of Noah who are going out of the ark are Shem, and Ham, and Japheth; and Ham is father of Canaan.
9.19: These three are sons of Noah, and from these has all the earth been overspread.
9.20: And Noah remains a man of the ground, and plants a vineyard,
9.21: and drinks of the wine, and is drunken, and uncovers himself in the midst of the tent.
9.22: And Ham, father of Canaan, sees the nakedness of his father, and declares to his two brethren without.
9.23: And Shem takes--Japheth also--the garment, and they place on the shoulder of them both, and go backward, and cover the nakedness of their father; and their faces are backward, and their father's nakedness they have not seen.
9.24: And Noah awakes from his wine, and knows that which his young son has done to him,
9.25: and says: `Cursed is Canaan, Servant of servants he is to his brethren.'
9.26: And he says: `Blessed of Jehovah my God is Shem, And Canaan is servant to him.
9.27: God does give beauty to Japheth, And he dwells in tents of Shem, And Canaan is servant to him.'
9.28: And Noah lives after the deluge three hundred and fifty years;
9.29: and all the days of Noah are nine hundred and fifty years, and he dies.

10.1: And these are births of the sons of Noah, Shem, Ham, and Japheth; and born to them are sons after the deluge.
10.2: `Sons of Japheth are Gomer, and Magog, and Madai, and Javan, and Tubal, and Meshech, and Tiras.
10.3: And sons of Gomer are Ashkenaz, and Riphath, and Togarmah.
10.4: And sons of Javan are Elishah, and Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.
10.5: By these have the isles of the nations been parted in their lands, each by his tongue, by their families, in their nations.
10.6: And sons of Ham are Cush, and Mitzraim, and Phut, and Canaan.
10.7: And sons of Cush are Seba, and Havilah, and Sabtah, and Raamah, and Sabtechah; and sons of Raamah are Sheba and Dedan.
10.9: he has begun to be a hero in the land; he has been a hero in hunting before Jehovah; therefore it is said, `As Nimrod the hero in hunting before Jehovah.'
10.10: And the first part of his kingdom is Babel, and Erech, and Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar;
10.11: from that land he has gone out to Asshur, and builds Nineveh, even the broad places of the city, and Calah,
10.12: and Resen, between Nineveh and Calah; it is the great city.
10.13: And Mitzraim has begotten the Ludim, and the Anamim, and the Lehabim, and the Naphtuhim,
10.14: and the Pathrusim, and the Casluhim, (from where have come out Philistim,) and the Caphtorim.
10.15: And Canaan has begotten Sidon his first-born, and Heth,
10.16: and the Jebusite, and the Amorite, and the Girgashite,
10.17: and the Hivite, and the Arkite, and the Sinite,
10.18: and the Arvadite, and the Zemarite, and the Hamathite; and afterwards have the families of the Canaanite been scattered.
10.19: And the border of the Canaanite is from Sidon, in your coming toward Gerar, to Gaza; in your coming toward Sodom, and Gomorrah, and Admah, and Zeboim, to Lasha.
10.20: These are sons of Ham, by their families, by their tongues, in their lands, in their nations.
10.21: As to Shem, father of all sons of Eber, brother of Japheth the elder, he has also begotten:
10.22: Sons of Shem are Elam, and Asshur, and Arphaxad, and Lud, and Aram.
10.23: And sons of Aram are Uz, and Hul, and Gether, and Mash.
10.24: And Arphaxad has begotten Salah, and Salah has begotten Eber.
10.25: And to Eber have two sons been born; the name of the one is Peleg (for in his days has the earth been divided,) and his brother's name is Joktan.
10.26: And Joktan has begotten Almodad, and Sheleph, and Hazarmaveth, and Jerah,
10.27: and Hadoram, and Uzal, and Diklah,
10.28: and Obal, and Abimael, and Sheba,
10.29: and Ophir, and Havilah, and Jobab; all these are sons of Joktan;
10.30: and their dwelling is from Mesha, in your coming toward Sephar, a mount of the east.
10.31: These are sons of Shem, by their families, by their tongues, in their lands, by their nations.
10.32: These are families of the sons of Noah, by their births, in their nations, and by these have the nations been parted in the earth after the deluge.

11.1: And the whole earth is of one pronunciation, and of the same words,
11.2: and it comes to pass, in their journeying from the east, that they find a valley in the land of Shinar, and dwell there;
11.3: and they say each one to his neighbour, `Give help, let us make bricks, and burn them thoroughly:' and the brick is to them for stone, and the bitumen has been to them for mortar.
11.4: And they say, `Give help, let us build for ourselves a city and tower, and its head in the heavens, and make for ourselves a name, lest we be scattered over the face of all the earth.'
11.5: And Jehovah comes down to see the city and the tower which the sons of men have builded;
11.6: and Jehovah says, `Indeed, the people is one, and one pronunciation is to them all, and this it has dreamed of doing; and now, nothing is restrained from them of that which they have purposed to do.
11.7: Give help, let us go down, and mingle there their pronunciation, so that a man does not understand the pronunciation of his companion.'
11.8: And Jehovah does scatter them from from there over the face of all the earth, and they cease to build the city;
11.9: therefore has one called its name Babel, for there has Jehovah mingled the pronunciation of all the earth, and from from there has Jehovah scattered them over the face of all the earth.
11.10: These are births of Shem: Shem is a son of an hundred years, and begets Arphaxad two years after the deluge.
11.11: And Shem lives after his begetting Arphaxad five hundred years, and begets sons and daughters.
11.12: And Arphaxad has lived five and thirty years, and begets Salah.
11.13: And Arphaxad lives after his begetting Salah four hundred and three years, and begets sons and daughters.
11.14: And Salah has lived thirty years, and begets Eber.
11.15: And Salah lives after his begetting Eber four hundred and three years, and begets sons and daughters.
11.16: And Eber lives four and thirty years, and begets Peleg.
11.17: And Eber lives after his begetting Peleg four hundred and thirty years, and begets sons and daughters.
11.18: And Peleg lives thirty years, and begets Reu.
11.19: And Peleg lives after his begetting Reu two hundred and nine years, and begets sons and daughters.
11.20: And Reu lives two and thirty years, and begets Serug.
11.21: And Reu lives after his begetting Serug two hundred and seven years, and begets sons and daughters.
11.22: And Serug lives thirty years, and begets Nahor.
11.23: And Serug lives after his begetting Nahor two hundred years, and begets sons and daughters.
11.24: And Nahor lives nine and twenty years, and begets Terah.
11.25: And Nahor lives after his begetting Terah an hundred and nineteen years, and begets sons and daughters.
11.26: And Terah lives seventy years, and begets Abram, Nahor, and Haran.
11.27: And these are births of Terah: Terah has begotten Abram, Nahor, and Haran; and Haran has begotten Lot;
11.28: and Haran dies in the presence of Terah his father, in the land of his birth, in Ur of the Chaldees.
11.29: And Abram and Nahor take to themselves wives; the name of Abram's wife is Sarai, and the name of Nahor's wife is Milcah, daughter of Haran, father of Milcah, and father of Iscah.
11.30: And Sarai is barren--she has no child.
11.31: And Terah takes Abram his son, and Lot, son of Haran, his son's son, and Sarai his daughter-in-law, wife of Abram his son, and they go out with them from Ur of the Chaldees, to go toward the land of Canaan; and they come to Charan, and dwell there.
11.32: And the days of Terah are two hundred and five years, and Terah dies in Charan.

12.1: And Jehovah says to Abram, `Go for yourself, from your land, and from your kindred, and from the house of your father, to the land which I show you.
12.2: And I make you become a great nation, and bless you, and make your name great; and be you a blessing.
12.3: And I bless those blessing you, and him who is disesteeming you I curse, and blessed in you have been all families of the ground.'
12.4: And Abram goes on, as Jehovah has spoken to him, and Lot goes with him, and Abram is a son of five and seventy years in his going out from Charan.
12.5: And Abram takes Sarai his wife, and Lot his brother's son, and all their substance that they have gained, and the persons that they have obtained in Charan; and they go out to go toward the land of Canaan; and they come in to the land of Canaan.
12.6: And Abram passes over into the land, to the place Shechem, to the oak of Moreh; and the Canaanite is then in the land.
12.7: And Jehovah appears to Abram, and says, `To your seed I give this land;' and he builds there an altar to Jehovah, who has appeared to him.
12.8: And he removes from from there toward a mountain at the east of Beth-El, and stretches out the tent (Beth-El at the west, and Hai at the east), and he builds there an altar to Jehovah, and preaches in the name of Jehovah.
12.9: And Abram journeys, going on and journeying toward the south.
12.10: And there is a famine in the land, and Abram goes down toward Egypt to sojourn there, for the famine is grievous in the land;
12.11: and it comes to pass as he has drawn near to enter Egypt, that he says to Sarai his wife, `Indeed, I pray you, I have known that you are a woman of beautiful appearance;
12.12: and it has come to pass that the Egyptians see you, and they have said, `This is his wife,' and they have slain me, and you they keep alive:
12.13: say, I pray you, you are my sister, so that it is well with me because of you, and my soul has lived for your sake.'
12.14: And it comes to pass, at the entering of Abram into Egypt, that the Egyptians see the woman that she is exceeding fair;
12.15: and princes of Pharaoh see her, and praise her to Pharaoh, and the woman is taken to Pharaoh's house;
12.16: and to Abram he has done good because of her, and he has sheep and oxen, and he-asses, and men-servants, and handmaids, and she-asses, and camels.
12.17: And Jehovah plagues Pharaoh and his house--great plagues--for the matter of Sarai, Abram's wife.
12.18: And Pharaoh calls for Abram, and says, `What is this you have done to me? why have you not declared to me that she is your wife?
12.19: Why have you said, She is my sister, and I take her to myself for a wife? and now, indeed, your wife, take and go.'
12.20: And Pharaoh charges men concerning him, and they send him away, and his wife, an all that he has.

13.1: And Abram goes up from Egypt (he and his wife, and all that he has, and Lot with him) toward the south;
13.2: and Abram is exceedingly wealthy in cattle, in silver, and in gold.
13.3: And he goes on his journeyings from the south, even to Bethel, to the place where his tent had been at the commencement, between Bethel and Hai--
13.4: to the place of the altar which he made there at the first, and there does Abram preach in the name of Jehovah.
13.5: And also to Lot, who is going with Abram, there has been sheep and oxen and tents;
13.6: and the land has not suffered them to dwell together, for their substance has been much, and they have not been able to dwell together;
13.7: and there is a strife between those feeding Abram's cattle and those feeding Lot's cattle; and the Canaanite and the Perizzite are then dwelling in the land.
13.8: And Abram says to Lot, `Let there not, I pray you, be strife between me and you, and between my shepherds and your shepherds, for we are men--brethren.
13.9: Is not all the land before you? be parted, I pray you, from me; if to the left, then I to the right; and if to the right, then I to the left.'
13.10: And Lot lifts up his eyes, and sees the whole circuit of the Jordan that it is all a watered country (before Jehovah's destroying Sodom and Gomorrah, as Jehovah's garden, as the land of Egypt,) in your coming toward Zoar,
13.11: and Lot chooses for himself the whole circuit of the Jordan; and Lot journeys from the east, and they are parted--a man from his companion;
13.12: Abram has dwelt in the land of Canaan, and Lot has dwelt in the cities of the circuit, and tents to Sodom;
13.13: and the men of Sodom are evil, and sinners before Jehovah exceedingly.
13.14: And Jehovah said to Abram, after Lot's being parted from him, `Lift up, I pray you, your eyes, and look from the place where you are, northward, and southward, and eastward, and westward;
13.15: for the whole of the land which you are seeing, to you I give it, and to your seed--to the age.
13.16: And I have set your seed as dust of the earth, so that, if one is able to number the dust of the earth, even your seed is numbered;
13.17: rise, go up and down through the land, to its length, and to its breadth, for to you I give it.'
13.18: And Abram tents, and comes, and dwells among the oaks of Mamre, which are in Hebron, and builds there an altar to Jehovah.

14.1: And it comes to pass in the days of Amraphel king of Shinar, Arioch king of Ellasar, Chedorlaomer king of Elam, and Tidal king of Goyim,
14.2: they have made war with Bera king of Sodom, and with Birsha king of Gomorrah, Shinab king of Admah, and Shemeber king of Zeboim, and the king of Bela, which is Zoar.
14.3: All these have been joined together to the valley of Siddim, which is the Salt Sea;
14.4: twelve years they served Chedorlaomer, and the thirteenth year they rebelled.
14.5: And in the fourteenth year came Chedorlaomer, and the kings who are with him, and they smite the Rephaim in Ashteroth Karnaim, and the Zuzim in Ham, and the Emim in Shaveh Kiriathaim,
14.6: and the Horites in their mount Seir, to El-Paran, which is by the wilderness;
14.7: and they turn back and come in to En-Mishpat, which is Kadesh, and smite the whole field of the Amalekite, and also the Amorite who is dwelling in Hazezon-Tamar.
14.8: And the king of Sodom goes out, and the king of Gomorrah, and the king of Admah, and the king of Zeboim, and the king of Bela, which is Zoar; and they set the battle in array with them in the valley of Siddim,
14.9: with Chedorlaomer king of Elam, and Tidal king of Goyim, and Amraphel king of Shinar, and Arioch king of Ellasar; four kings with the five.
14.10: And the valley of Siddim is full of bitumen-pits; and the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah flee, and fall there, and those left have fled to the mountain.
14.11: And they take the whole substance of Sodom and Gomorrah, and the whole of their food, and go away;
14.12: and they take Lot, Abram's brother's son (seeing he is dwelling in Sodom), and his substance, and go away.
14.13: And one who is escaping comes and declares to Abram the Hebrew, and he is dwelling among the oaks of Mamre the Amorite, brother of Eshcol, and brother of Aner, and they are Abram's allies.
14.14: And Abram hears that his brother has been taken captive, and he draws out his trained domestics, three hundred and eighteen, and pursues to Dan.
14.15: And he divides himself against them by night, he and his servants, and smites them, and pursues them to Hobah, which is at the left of Damascus;
14.16: and he brings back the whole of the substance, and also Lot his brother and his substance has he brought back, and also the women and the people.
14.17: And the king of Sodom goes out to meet him (after his turning back from the smiting of Chedorlaomer, and of the kings who are with him), to the valley of Shaveh, which is the king's valley.
14.18: And Melchizedek king of Salem has brought out bread and wine, and he is priest of God Most High;
14.19: and he blesses him, and says, `Blessed is Abram to God Most High, possessing heaven and earth;
14.20: and blessed is God Most High, who has delivered your adversaries into your hand;' and he gives to him a tenth of all.
14.21: And the king of Sodom says to Abram, `Give to me the persons, and the substance take to yourself,'
14.22: and Abram says to the king of Sodom, `I have lifted up my hand to Jehovah, God Most High, possessing heaven and earth--
14.23: from a thread even to a shoe-latchet I take not of anything which you have, that you say not, I--I have made Abram rich;
14.24: save only that which the young men have eaten, and the portion of the men who have gone with me--Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre--they take their portion.'

15.1: After these things has the word of Jehovah been to Abram in a vision, saying, `Fear not, Abram, I am a shield to you, your reward is exceeding great.'
15.2: And Abram says, `Lord Jehovah, what do You give to me, and I am going childless? and an acquired son in my house is Demmesek Eliezer.'
15.3: And Abram says, `Indeed, to me You have not given seed, and indeed, a domestic does heir me.'
15.4: And indeed, the word of Jehovah is to him, saying, `This one does not heir you; but he who comes out from your bowels, he does heir you;'
15.5: and He brings him out without, and says, `Look attentively, I pray you, toward the heavens, and count the stars, if you are able to count them;' and He says to him, `Thus is your seed.'
15.6: And he has believed in Jehovah, and He reckons it to him--righteousness.
15.7: And He says to him, `I am Jehovah who brought you out from Ur of the Chaldees, to give to you this land to possess it;'
15.8: and he says, `Lord Jehovah, by which do I know that I possess it?'
15.9: And He says to him, `Take for Me a heifer of three years, and a she-goat of three years, and a ram of three years, and a turtle-dove, and a young bird;'
15.10: and he takes to him all these, and separates them in the midst, and puts each piece over against its fellow, but the bird he has not divided;
15.11: and the ravenous birds come down upon the carcases, and Abram causes them to turn back.
15.12: And the sun is about to go in, and deep sleep has fallen upon Abram, and indeed, a terror of great darkness is falling upon him;
15.13: and He says to Abram, `knowing--know that your seed is a sojourner in a land not theirs, and they have served them, and they have afflicted them four hundred years,
15.14: and the nation also whom they serve I judge, and after this they go out with great substance;
15.15: and you--you come in to your fathers in peace; you are buried in a good old age;
15.16: and the fourth generation does turn back here, for the iniquity of the Amorite is not yet complete.'
15.17: And it comes to pass--the sun has gone in, and thick darkness has been--and indeed, a furnace of smoke, and a lamp of fire, which has passed over between those pieces.
15.18: In that day has Jehovah made with Abram a covenant, saying, `To your seed I have given this land, from the river of Egypt to the great river, the river Phrat,
15.19: with the Kenite, and the Kenizzite, and the Kadmonite,
15.20: and the Hittite, and the Perizzite, and the Rephaim,
15.21: and the Amorite, and the Canaanite, and the Girgashite, and the Jebusite.'

16.1: And Sarai, Abram's wife, has not borne to him, and she has an handmaid, an Egyptian, and her name is Hagar;
16.2: and Sarai says to Abram, `Indeed, I pray you, Jehovah has restrained me from bearing, go in, I pray you, to my handmaid; perhaps I am built up from her;' and Abram hearkens to the voice of Sarai.
16.3: And Sarai, Abram's wife, takes Hagar the Egyptian, her handmaid, at the end of the tenth year of Abram's dwelling in the land of Canaan, and gives her to Abram her husband, to him for a wife,
16.4: and he goes in to Hagar, and she conceives, and she sees that she has conceived, and her mistress is lightly esteemed in her eyes.
16.5: And Sarai says to Abram, `My violence is for you; I--I have given my handmaid into your bosom, and she sees that she has conceived, and I am lightly esteemed in her eyes; Jehovah does judge between me and you.'
16.6: And Abram says to Sarai, `Indeed, your handmaid is in your hand, do to her that which is good in your eyes;' and Sarai afflicted her, and she flees from her presence.
16.7: And a messenger of Jehovah finds her by the fountain of water in the wilderness, by the fountain in the way to Shur,
16.8: and he says, `Hagar, Sarai's handmaid, from where have you come, and where do you go?' and she says, `From the presence of Sarai, my mistress, I am fleeing.'
16.9: And the messenger of Jehovah says to her, `Turn back to your mistress, and humble yourself under her hands;'
16.10: and the messenger of Jehovah says to her, `Multiplying I multiply your seed, and it is not numbered from multitude;'
16.11: and the messenger of Jehovah says to her, `Behold you are conceiving, and bearing a son, and have called his name Ishmael, for Jehovah has hearkened to your affliction;
16.12: and he is a wild-ass man, his hand against every one, and every one's hand against him--and before the face of all his brethren he dwells.'
16.13: And she calls the name of Jehovah who is speaking to her, `You are, O God, my beholder;' for she said, `Even here have I looked behind my beholder?'
16.14: therefore has one called the well, `The well of the Living One, my beholder;' indeed, between Kadesh and Bered.
16.15: And Hagar bears to Abram a son; and Abram calls the name of his son, whom Hagar has borne, Ishmael;
16.16: and Abram is a son of eighty and six years in Hagar's bearing Ishmael to Abram.

17.1: And Abram is a son of ninety and nine years, and Jehovah appears to Abram, and says to him, `I am God Almighty, walk habitually before Me, and be you perfect;
17.2: and I give My covenant between Me and you, and multiply you very exceedingly.'
17.3: And Abram falls upon his face, and God speaks with him, saying,
17.4: `I--indeed, My covenant is with you, and you have become father of a multitude of nations;
17.5: and your name is no more called Abram, but your name has been Abraham, for father of a multitude of nations have I made you;
17.6: and I have made you exceeding fruitful, and made you become nations, and kings go out from you.
17.7: `And I have established My covenant between Me and you, and your seed after you, to their generations, for a covenant age-during, to become God to you, and to your seed after you;
17.8: and I have given to you, and to your seed after you, the land of your sojournings, the whole land of Canaan, for a possession age-during, and I have become their God.'
17.9: And God says to Abraham, `And you do keep My covenant, you and your seed after you, to their generations;
17.10: this is My covenant which you keep between Me and you, and your seed after you: Every male of you is to be circumcised;
17.11: and you have circumcised the flesh of your foreskin, and it has become a token of a covenant between Me and you.
17.12: `And a son of eight days is circumcised by you; every male to your generations, born in the house, or bought with money from any son of a stranger, who is not of your seed;
17.13: he is certainly circumcised who is born in your house, or bought with your money; and My covenant has become in your flesh a covenant age-during;
17.14: and an uncircumcised one, a male, the flesh of whose foreskin is not circumcised, even that person has been cut off from his people; My covenant he has broken.'
17.15: And God says to Abraham, `Sarai your wife--you do not call her name Sarai, for Sarah is her name;
17.16: and I have blessed her, and have also given to you a son from her; and I have blessed her, and she has become nations--kings of peoples are from her.'
17.17: And Abraham falls upon his face, and laughs, and says in his heart, `To the son of an hundred years is one born? or does Sarah--daughter of ninety years--bear?'
17.18: And Abraham says to God, `O that Ishmael may live before You;'
17.19: and God says, `Sarah your wife is certainly bearing a son to you, and you have called his name Isaac, and I have established My covenant with him, for a covenant age-during, to his seed after him.
17.20: As to Ishmael, I have heard you; indeed, I have blessed him, and made him fruitful, and multiplied him, very exceedingly; twelve princes does he beget, and I have made him become a great nation;
17.21: and My covenant I establish with Isaac, whom Sarah does bear to you at this appointed time in the next year;'
17.22: and He finishes speaking with him, and God goes up from Abraham.
17.23: And Abraham takes Ishmael his son, and all those born in his house, and all those bought with his money--every male among the men of Abraham's house--and circumcises the flesh of their foreskin, in this self-same day, as God has spoken with him.
17.24: And Abraham is a son of ninety and nine years in the flesh of his foreskin being circumcised;
17.25: and Ishmael his son is a son of thirteen years in the flesh of his foreskin being circumcised;
17.26: in this self-same day has Abraham been circumcised, and Ishmael his son;
17.27: and all the men of his house--born in the house, and bought with money from the son of a stranger--have been circumcised with him.

18.1: And Jehovah appears to him among the oaks of Mamre, and he is sitting at the opening of the tent, about the heat of the day;
18.2: and he lifts up his eyes and looks, and indeed, three men standing by him, and he sees, and runs to meet them from the opening of the tent, and bows himself toward the earth,
18.3: And he says, `My Lord, if, I pray you, I have found grace in your eyes, do not, I pray you, pass on from your servant;
18.4: let, I pray you, a little water be accepted, and wash your feet, and recline under the tree;
18.5: and I bring a piece of bread, and support you your heart; afterwards pass on, for therefore have you passed over to your servant;' and they say, `So may you do as you has spoken.'
18.6: And Abraham hastes toward the tent, to Sarah, and says, `Hasten three measures of flour-meal, knead, and make cakes;'
18.7: and Abraham ran to the herd, and takes a son of the herd, tender and good, and gives to the young man, and he hastes to prepare it;
18.8: and he takes butter and milk, and the son of the herd which he has prepared, and sets before them; and he is standing by them under the tree, and they do eat.
18.9: And they say to him, `Where is Sarah your wife?' and he says, `Indeed--in the tent;'
18.10: and he says, `returning I return to you, about the time of life, and indeed, to Sarah your wife a son.'
18.11: And Sarah is hearkening at the opening of the tent, which is behind him;
18.12: and Abraham and Sarah are aged, entering into days--the way of women has ceased to be to Sarah;
18.13: and Sarah laughs in her heart, saying, `After I have waxed old I have had pleasure! --my lord also is old!'
18.14: And Jehovah says to Abraham, `Why is this? Sarah has laughed, saying, Is it true really--I bear--and I am aged? Is any thing too wonderful for Jehovah? at the appointed time I return to you, about the time of life, and Sarah has a son.'
18.15: And Sarah denies, saying, `I did not laugh;' for she has been afraid; and He says, `No, but you did laugh.'
18.16: And the men rise from from there, and look on the face of Sodom, and Abraham is going with them to send them away;
18.17: and Jehovah said, `Am I concealing from Abraham that which I am doing,
18.18: and Abraham certainly becomes a nation great and mighty, and blessed in him have been all nations of the earth?
18.19: for I have known him, that he commands his children, and his house after him (and they have kept the way of Jehovah), to do righteousness and judgment, that Jehovah may bring on Abraham that which He has spoken concerning him.'
18.20: And Jehovah says, `The cry of Sodom and Gomorrah--because great; and their sin--because exceeding grievous:
18.21: I go down now, and see whether according to its cry which is coming to Me they have done completely--and if not--I know;'
18.22: and the men turn from from there, and go toward Sodom; and Abraham is yet standing before Jehovah.
18.23: And Abraham draws nigh and says, `Do You also consume righteous with wicked?
18.24: perhaps there are fifty righteous in the midst of the city; do You also consume, and not bear with the place for the sake of the fifty--the righteous who are in its midst?
18.25: Far be it from You to do according to this thing, to put to death the righteous with the wicked; that it has been--as the righteous so the wicked--far be it from You; does the Judge of all the earth not do justice?'
18.26: And Jehovah says, `If I find in Sodom fifty righteous in the midst of the city, then have I borne with all the place for their sake.'
18.27: And Abraham answers and says, `Indeed, I pray you, I have willed to speak to the Lord, and I--dust and ashes;
18.28: perhaps there are lacking five of the fifty righteous--do You destroy for five the whole of the city?' and He says, `I destroy it not, if I find there forty and five.'
18.29: And he adds again to speak to Him and says, `Perhaps there are found there forty?' and He says, `I do it not, because of the forty.'
18.30: And he says, `Let it not be, I Pray you, displeasing to the Lord, and I speak: perhaps there are found there thirty?' and He says, `I do it not, if I find there thirty.'
18.31: And he says, `Indeed, I pray you, I have willed to speak to the Lord: perhaps there are found there twenty?' and He says, `I do not destroy it, because of the twenty.'
18.32: And he says, `Let it not be, I pray You, displeasing to the Lord, and I speak only this time: perhaps there are found there ten?' and He says, `I do not destroy it, because of the ten.'
18.33: And Jehovah goes on, when He has finished speaking to Abraham, and Abraham has turned back to his place.

19.1: And two of the messengers come toward Sodom at even, and Lot is sitting at the gate of Sodom, and Lot sees, and rises to meet them, and bows himself--face to the earth,
19.2: and he says, `Indeed, I pray you, my lords, turn aside, I pray you, to the house of your servant, and lodge, and wash your feet--then you have risen early and gone on your way;' and they say, `No, but in the broad place we do lodge.'
19.3: And he presses on them greatly, and they turn aside to him, and come in to his house; and he makes for them a banquet, and has baked unleavened things; and they do eat.
19.4: Before they lie down, the men of the city--men of Sodom--have come round about against the house, from young even to aged, all the people from the extremity;
19.5: and they call to Lot and say to him, `Where are the men who have come in to you to-night? bring them out to us, and we know them.'
19.6: And Lot goes out to them, to the opening, and the door has shut behind him,
19.7: and says, `Do not, I pray you, my brethren, do evil;
19.8: indeed, I pray you, I have two daughters, who have not known any one; let me, I pray you, bring them out to you, and do to them as is good in your eyes; only to these men do not anything, for therefore have they come in within the shadow of my roof.'
19.9: And they say, `Come nigh here;' they say also, `This one has come in to sojourn, and he certainly judges! now, we do evil to you more than to them;' and they press against the man, against Lot greatly, and come nigh to break the door.
19.10: And the men put forth their hand, and bring in Lot to them, into the house, and have shut the door;
19.11: and the men who are at the opening of the house they have smitten with blindness, from small even to great, and they weary themselves to find the opening.
19.12: And the men say to Lot, `Whom have you here still? son-in-law, your sons also, and your daughters, and all whom you have in the city, bring out from this place;
19.13: for we are destroying this place, for their cry has been great before the face of Jehovah, and Jehovah does send us to destroy it.'
19.14: And Lot goes out, and speaks to his sons-in-law, those taking his daughters, and says, `Rise, go out from this place, for Jehovah is destroying the city;' and he is as one mocking in the eyes of his sons-in-law.
19.15: And when the dawn has ascended, then the messengers press upon Lot, saying, `Rise, take your wife, and your two daughters who are found present, lest you be consumed in the iniquity of the city.'
19.16: And he lingers, and the men lay hold on his hand, and on the hand of his wife, and on the hand of his two daughters, through the mercy of Jehovah to him, and they bring him out, and cause him to rest without the city.
19.17: And it comes to pass when he has brought them out without, that he says, `Escape for your life; look not expectingly behind you, nor stand you in all the circuit; to the mountain escape, lest you be consumed.'
19.18: And Lot says to them, `Not so, I pray you, my lord;
19.19: indeed, I pray you, your servant has found grace in your eyes, and you do make great your kindness which you have done with me by saving my life, and I am unable to escape to the mountain, lest the evil cleave to me, and I have died;
19.20: indeed, I pray you, this city is near to flee there, and it is little; let me escape, I pray you, there, (is it not little?) and my soul does live.'
19.21: And he says to him, `Indeed, I have accepted your face also for this thing, without overthrowing the city for which you have spoken;
19.22: haste, escape there, for I am not able to do anything till your entering there;' therefore has he calls the name of the city Zoar.
19.23: The sun has gone out on the earth, and Lot has entered into Zoar,
19.24: and Jehovah has rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire from Jehovah, from the heavens;
19.25: and He overthrows these cities, and all the circuit, and all the inhabitants of the cities, and that which is shooting up from the ground.
19.26: And his wife looks expectingly from behind him, and she is--a pillar of salt!
19.27: And Abraham rises early in the morning, to the place where he has stood before the face of Jehovah;
19.28: and he looks on the face of Sodom and Gomorrah, and on all the face of the land of the circuit, and sees, and indeed, the smoke of the land went up as smoke of the furnace.
19.29: And it comes to pass, in God's destroying the cities of the circuit, that God remembers Abraham, and sends Lot out of the midst of the overthrow in the overthrowing of the cities in which Lot dwelt.
19.30: And Lot goes up out of Zoar, and dwells in the mountain, and his two daughters with him, for he has been afraid of dwelling in Zoar, and he dwells in a cave, he and his two daughters.
19.31: And the first-born says to the younger, `Our father is old, and a man there is not in the earth to come in to us, as is the way of all the earth;
19.32: come, we cause our father to drink wine, and lie with him, and preserve from our father--a seed.'
19.33: And they cause their father to drink wine on that night; and the first-born goes in, and lies with her father, and he has not known in her lying down, or in her rising up.
19.34: And it comes to pass, on the morrow, that the first-born says to the younger, `Indeed, I have lain yesterday-night with my father: we cause him to drink wine also to-night, and go you in, lie with him, and we preserve from our father--a seed.'
19.35: And they cause their father to drink wine on that night also, and the younger rises and lies with him, and he has not known in her lying down, or in her rising up.
19.36: And the two daughters of Lot conceive from their father,
19.37: and the first-born bears a son, and calls his name Moab; he is father of Moab to this day;
19.38: as to the younger, she also has born a son, and calls his name Ben-Ammi: he is father of the Beni-Ammon to this day.

20.1: And Abraham journeys from from there toward the land of the south, and dwells between Kadesh and Shur, and sojourns in Gerar;
20.2: and Abraham says concerning Sarah his wife, `She is my sister;' and Abimelech king of Gerar sends and takes Sarah.
20.3: And God comes in to Abimelech in a dream of the night, and says to him, `Indeed, you are a dead man, because of the woman whom you have taken--and she married to a husband.'
20.4: And Abimelech has not drawn near to her, and he says, `Lord, also a righteous nation do you slay?
20.5: has not he himself said to me, She is my sister! and she, even she herself, said, He is my brother; in the integrity of my heart, and in the innocency of my hands, I have done this.'
20.6: And God says to him in the dream, `Yes, I--I have known that in the integrity of your heart you have done this, and I withhold you, even I, from sinning against Me, therefore I have not suffered you to come against her;
20.7: and now send back the man's wife, for he is inspired, and he does pray for you, and live you; and if you do not send back, know that dying you do die, you, and all that you have.'
20.8: And Abimelech rises early in the morning, and calls for all his servants, and speaks all these words in their ears; and the men fear exceedingly;
20.9: and Abimelech calls for Abraham, and says to him, `What have you done to us? and what have I sinned against you, that you have brought upon me, and upon my kingdom, a great sin? works which are not done you have done with me.'
20.10: Abimelech also says to Abraham, `What have you seen that you have done this thing?'
20.11: And Abraham says, `Because I said, `Surely the fear of God is not in this place, and they have slain me for the sake of my wife;
20.12: and also, truly she is my sister, daughter of my father, only not daughter of my mother, and she becomes my wife;
20.13: and it comes to pass, when God has caused me to wander from my father's house, that I say to her, This is your kindness which you do with me: at every place where we come, say of me, He is my brother.'
20.14: And Abimelech takes sheep and oxen, and servants and handmaids, and gives to Abraham, and sends back to him Sarah his wife;
20.15: and Abimelech says, `Indeed, my land is before you, where it is good in your eyes, dwell;'
20.16: and to Sarah he has said, `Indeed, I have given a thousand silverlings to your brother; indeed, it is to you a covering of eyes, to all who are with you;' and by all this she is reasoned with.
20.17: And Abraham prays to God, and God heals Abimelech and his wife, and his handmaids, and they bear:
20.18: for Jehovah restraining had restrained every womb of the house of Abimelech, because of Sarah, Abraham's wife.

21.1: And Jehovah has looked after Sarah as He has said, and Jehovah does to Sarah as He has spoken;
21.2: and Sarah conceives, and bears a son to Abraham, to his old age, at the appointed time that God has spoken of with him;
21.3: and Abraham calls the name of his son who is born to him, whom Sarah has born to him--Isaac;
21.4: and Abraham circumcises Isaac his son, being a son of eight days, as God has commanded him.
21.5: And Abraham is a son of a hundred years in Isaac his son being born to him,
21.6: and Sarah says, `God has made laughter for me; every one who is hearing laughs for me.'
21.7: She says also, `Who has said to Abraham, Sarah has suckled sons, that I have born a son for his old age?'
21.8: And the lad grows, and is weaned, and Abraham makes a great banquet in the day of Isaac's being weaned;
21.9: and Sarah sees the son of Hagar the Egyptian, whom she has borne to Abraham, mocking,
21.10: and she says to Abraham, `Cast out this handmaid and her son; for the son of this handmaid has no possession with my son--with Isaac.'
21.11: And the thing is very wrong in the eyes of Abraham, for his son's sake;
21.12: and God says to Abraham, `Let it not be wrong in your eyes because of the youth, and because of your handmaid: all that Sarah says to you--hearken to her voice, for in Isaac is a seed called to you.
21.13: As to the son of the handmaid also, for a nation I set him, because he is your seed.'
21.14: And Abraham rises early in the morning, and takes bread, and a bottle of water, and gives to Hagar (placing it on her shoulder), also the lad, and sends her out; and she goes on, and goes astray in the wilderness of Beer-Sheba;
21.15: and the water is consumed from the bottle, and she places the lad under one of the shrubs.
21.16: And she goes and sits by herself over-against, afar off, about a bow-shot, for she said, `Let me not look on the death of the lad;' and she sits over-against, and lifts up her voice, and weeps.
21.17: And God hears the voice of the youth; and the messenger of God calls to Hagar from the heavens, and says to her, `What to you, Hagar? fear not; for God has hearkened to the voice of the youth where he is;
21.18: rise, lift up the youth, and lay hold on him with your hand, for for a great nation I set him.'
21.19: And God opens her eyes, and she sees a well of water, and she goes and fills the bottle with water, and causes the youth to drink;
21.20: and God is with the youth, and he grows, and dwells in the wilderness, and is an archer;
21.21: and he dwells in the wilderness of Paran, and his mother takes for him a wife from the land of Egypt.
21.22: And it comes to pass at that time that Abimelech speaks--Phichol also, head of his host--to Abraham, saying, `God is with you in all that you are doing;
21.23: and now, swear to me by God here: you do not lie to me, or to my continuator, or to my successor; according to the kindness which I have done with you you do with me, and with the land in which you have sojourned.'
21.25: And Abraham reasoned with Abimelech concerning the matter of a well of water which Abimelech's servants have taken violently away,
21.26: and Abimelech says, `I have not known who has done this thing, and even you did not declare to me, and I also, I have not heard save to-day.'
21.27: And Abraham takes sheep and oxen, and gives to Abimelech, and they make, both of them, a covenant;
21.28: and Abraham sets seven Lambs of the flock by themselves.
21.29: And Abimelech says to Abraham, `What are they--these seven lambs which you have set by themselves?'
21.30: And he says, `For--the seven lambs you do accept from my hand, so that it becomes a witness for me that I have digged this well;'
21.31: therefore has he called that place `Beer-Sheba,' for there have both of them sworn.
21.32: And they make a covenant in Beer-Sheba, and Abimelech rises--Phichol also, head of his host--and they turn back to the land of the Philistines;
21.33: and Abraham plants a tamarisk in Beer-Sheba, and preaches there in the name of Jehovah, God age-during;
21.34: and Abraham sojourns in the land of the Philistines many days.

22.1: And it comes to pass after these things that God has tried Abraham, and says to him, `Abraham;' and he says, `Here am I.'
22.2: And He says, `Take, I pray you, your son, your only one, whom you have loved, even Isaac, and go for yourself to the land of Moriah, and cause him to ascend there for a burnt-offering on one of the mountains of which I speak to you.'
22.3: And Abraham rises early in the morning, and saddles his ass, and takes two of his young men with him, and Isaac his son, and he cleaves the wood of the burnt-offering, and rises and goes to the place of which God has spoken to him.
22.4: On the third day--Abraham lifts up his eyes, and sees the place from afar;
22.5: and Abraham says to his young men, `Remain by yourselves here with the ass, and I and the youth go yonder and worship, and turn back to you.'
22.6: And Abraham takes the wood of the burnt-offering, and places on Isaac his son, and he takes in his hand the fire, and the knife; and they go on both of them together.
22.7: And Isaac speaks to Abraham his father, and says, `My father,' and he says, `Here am I, my son.' And he says, `Indeed, the fire and the wood, and where the lamb for a burnt-offering?'
22.8: and Abraham says, `God does provide for Himself the lamb for a burnt-offering, my son;' and they go on both of them together.
22.9: And they come in to the place of which God has spoken to him, and there Abraham builds the altar, and arranges the wood, and binds Isaac his son, and places him upon the altar above the wood;
22.10: and Abraham puts forth his hand, and takes the knife--to slaughter his son.
22.11: And the messenger of Jehovah calls to him from the heavens, and says, `Abraham, Abraham;' and he says, `Here am I;'
22.12: and He says, `Put not forth your hand to the youth, nor do anything to him, for now I have known that you are fearing God, and have not withheld your son, your only one, from Me.'
22.13: And Abraham lifts up his eyes, and looks, and indeed, a ram behind, seized in a thicket by its horns; and Abraham goes, and takes the ram, and causes it to ascend for a burnt-offering instead of his son;
22.14: and Abraham calls the name of that place `Jehovah-Jireh,' because it is said this day in the mount, `Jehovah does provide.'
22.15: And the messenger of Jehovah calls to Abraham a second time from the heavens,
22.16: and says, `By Myself I have sworn--the affirmation of Jehovah--that because you have done this thing, and have not withheld your son, your only one--
22.17: that blessing I bless you, and multiplying I multiply your seed as stars of the heavens, and as sand which is on the sea-shore; and your seed does possess the gate of his enemies;
22.18: and blessed themselves in your seed have all nations of the earth, because that you have hearkened to My voice.'
22.19: And Abraham turns back to his young men, and they rise and go together to Beer-Sheba; and Abraham dwells in Beer-Sheba.
22.20: And it comes to pass after these things that it is declared to Abraham, saying, `Indeed, Milcah has borne, even she, sons to Nahor your brother:
22.21: Huz his first-born, and Buz his brother; and Kemuel father of Aram,
22.22: and Chesed, and Hazo, and Pildash, and Jidlaph, and Bethuel;
22.23: and Bethuel has begotten Rebekah;' these eight has Milcah borne to Nahor, Abraham's brother;
22.24: and his concubine, whose name is Reumah, she also has borne Tebah, and Gaham, and Tahash, and Maachah.

23.1: And the life of Sarah is a hundred and twenty and seven years--years of the life of Sarah;
23.2: and Sarah dies in Kirjath-Arba, which is Hebron, in the land of Caanan, and Abraham goes in to mourn for Sarah, and to bewail her.
23.3: And Abraham rises up from the presence of his dead, and speaks to the sons of Heth, saying,
23.4: `A sojourner and a settler I am with you; give to me a possession of a burying-place with you, and I bury my dead from before me.'
23.5: And the sons of Heth answer Abraham, saying to him,
23.6: `Hear us, my lord; a prince of God are you in our midst; in the choice of our burying-places bury your dead: none of us his burying-place does withhold from you, from burying your dead.'
23.7: And Abraham rises and bows himself to the people of the land, to the sons of Heth,
23.8: and he speaks with them, saying, `If it is your desire to bury my dead from before me, hear me, and meet for me with Ephron, son of Zoar;
23.9: and he gives to me the cave of Machpelah, which he has, which is in the extremity of his field; for full money does he give it to me, in your midst, for a possession of a burying-place.'
23.10: And Ephron is sitting in the midst of the sons of Heth, and Ephron the Hittite answers Abraham in the ears of the sons of Heth, of all those entering the gate of his city, saying,
23.11: `No, my lord, hear me: the field I have given to you, and the cave that is in it, to you I have given it; before the eyes of the sons of my people I have given it to you--bury your dead.'
23.12: And Abraham bows himself before the people of the land,
23.13: and speaks to Ephron in the ears of the people of the land, saying, `Only--if you would hear me--I have given the money of the field--accept from me, and I bury my dead there.'
23.14: And Ephron answers Abraham, saying to him,
23.15: `My lord, hear me: the land--four hundred shekels of silver; between me and you, what is it? --your dead bury.'
23.16: And Abraham hearkens to Ephron, and Abraham weighs to Ephron the silver which he has spoken of in the ears of the sons of Heth, four hundred silver shekels, passing with the merchant.
23.17: And established are the field of Ephron, which is in Machpelah, which is before Mamre, the field and the cave which is in it, and all the trees which are in the field, which are in all its border round about,
23.18: to Abraham by purchase, before the eyes of the sons of Heth, among all entering the gate of his city.
23.19: And after this has Abraham buried Sarah his wife at the cave of the field of Machpelah before Mamre (which is Hebron), in the land of Canaan;
23.20: and established are the field, and the cave which is in it, to Abraham for a possession of a burying-place, from the sons of Heth.

24.1: And Abraham is old, he has entered into days, and Jehovah has blessed Abraham in all things;
24.2: and Abraham says to his servant, the eldest of his house, who is ruling over all that he has, `Put, I pray you, your hand under my thigh,
24.3: and I cause you to swear by Jehovah, God of the heavens, and God of the earth, that you do not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanite, in the midst of whom I am dwelling;
24.4: but to my land and to my kindred do you go, and have taken a wife for my son, for Isaac.'
24.5: And the servant says to him, `It may be the woman is not willing to come after me to this land; do I at all cause your son to turn back to the land from from where you came out?'
24.6: And Abraham says to him, `Take heed to yourself, lest you cause my son to turn back there;
24.7: Jehovah, God of the heavens, who has taken me from the house of my father, and from the land of my birth, and who has spoken to me, and who has sworn to me, saying, To your seed I give this land, He does send His messenger before you, and you have taken a wife for my son from from there;
24.8: and if the woman be not willing to come after you, then you have been acquitted from this my oath: only my son you do not cause to turn back there.'
24.9: And the servant puts his hand under the thigh of Abraham his lord, and swears to him concerning this matter.
24.10: And the servant takes ten camels of the camels of his lord and goes, also of all the goods of his lord in his hand, and he rises, and goes to Aram-Naharaim, to the city of Nahor;
24.11: and he causes the camels to kneel at the outside of the city, at the well of water, at even-time, at the time of the coming out of the women who draw water.
24.12: And he says, `Jehovah, God of my lord Abraham, cause to meet, I pray You, before me this day--(and do kindness with my lord Abraham;
24.13: indeed, I am standing by the fountain of water, and daughters of the men of the city are coming out to draw water;
