24.14: and it has been, the young person to whom I say, Incline, I pray you, your pitcher, and I drink, and she has said, Drink, and I water also your camels) --her You have decided for Your servant, for Isaac; and by it I know that You have done kindness with my lord.'
24.15: And it comes to pass, before he has finished speaking, that indeed, Rebekah (who was born to Bethuel, son of Milcah, wife of Nahor, brother of Abraham) is coming out, and her pitcher on her shoulder,
24.16: and the young person is of very good appearance, a virgin, and a man has not known her; and she goes down to the fountain, and fills her pitcher, and comes up.
24.17: And the servant runs to meet her, and says, `Let me swallow, I pray you, a little water from your pitcher;'
24.18: and she says, `Drink, my lord;' and she hastes, and lets down her pitcher upon her hand, and gives him drink.
24.19: And she finishes giving him drink, and says, `Also for your camels I draw till they have finished drinking;'
24.20: and she hastes, and empties her pitcher into the drinking-trough, and runs again to the well to draw, and draws for all his camels.
24.21: And the man, wondering at her, remains silent, to know whether Jehovah has made his way prosperous or not.
24.22: And it comes to pass when the camels have finished drinking, that the man takes a golden ring (whose weight is a bekah), and two bracelets for her hands (whose weight is ten bekahs of gold),
24.23: and says, `Whose daughter are you? declare to me, I pray you, is the house of your father a place for us to lodge in?'
24.24: And she says to him, `I am daughter of Bethuel, son of Milcah, whom she has borne to Nahor.'
24.25: She says also to him, `Both straw and provender are abundant with us, also a place to lodge in.'
24.26: And the man bows, and does obeisance to Jehovah,
24.27: and says, `Blessed is Jehovah, God of my lord Abraham, who has not left off His kindness and His truth with my lord; --I being in the way, Jehovah has led me to the house of my lord's brethren.'
24.28: And the young person runs, and declares to the house of her mother according to these words.
24.29: And Rebekah has a brother, and his name is Laban, and Laban runs to the man who is without, to the fountain;
24.30: yes, it comes to pass, when he sees the ring, and the bracelets on the hands of his sister, and when he hears the words of Rebekah his sister, saying, `Thus has the man spoken to me,' that he comes in to the man, and indeed, he is standing by the camels by the fountain.
24.31: And he says, `Come in, O blessed one of Jehovah, why do you stand without, and I--I have prepared the house and place for the camels!'
24.32: And he brings in the man into the house, and looses the camels, and gives straw and provender for the camels, and water to wash his feet, and the feet of the men who are with him:
24.33: and sets before him to eat; but he says, `I do not eat till I have spoken my word;' and he says, `Speak.'
24.34: And he says, `I am Abraham's servant;
24.35: and Jehovah has blessed my lord exceedingly, and he is great; and He gives to him flock, and herd, and silver, and gold, and men-servants, and maid-servants, and camels, and asses;
24.36: and Sarah, my lord's wife, bears a son to my lord, after she has been aged, and he gives to him all that he has.
24.37: `And my lord causes me to swear, saying, You do not take a wife to my son from the daughters of the Canaanite, in whose land I am dwelling.
24.38: If not--to the house of my father you do go, and to my family, and you have taken a wife for my son.
24.39: `And I say to my lord, It may be the woman does not come after me;
24.40: and he says to me, Jehovah, before whom I have walked habitually, does send His messenger with you, and has prospered your way, and you have taken a wife for my son from my family, and from the house of my father;
24.41: then are you acquitted from my oath, when you come to my family, and if they give not one to you; then you have been acquitted from my oath.
24.42: `And I come to-day to the fountain, and I say, Jehovah, God of my lord Abraham, if You are, I pray You, making prosperous my way in which I am going--
24.43: (indeed, I am standing by the fountain of water), then the virgin who is coming out to draw, and I have said to her, Let me drink, I pray you, a little water from your pitcher,
24.44: and she has said to me, Both drink you, and also for your camels I draw--she is the woman whom Jehovah has decided for my lord's son.
24.45: `Before I finish speaking to my heart, then indeed, Rebekah is coming out, and her pitcher on her shoulder, and she goes down to the fountain, and draws; and I say to her, Let me drink, I pray you,
24.46: and she hastes and lets down her pitcher from off her and says, Drink, and your camels also I water; and I drink, and the camels also she has watered.
24.47: `And I ask her, and say, Whose daughter are you? and she says, Daughter of Bethuel, son of Nahor, whom Milcah has borne to him, and I put the ring on her nose, and the bracelets on her hands,
24.48: and I bow, and do obeisance before Jehovah, and I bless Jehovah, God of my lord Abraham, who has led me in the true way to receive the daughter of my lord's brother for his son.
24.49: `And now, if you are dealing kindly and truly with my lord, declare to me; and if not, declare to me; and I turn to the right or to the left.'
24.50: And Laban answers--Bethuel also--and they say, `The thing has gone out from Jehovah; we are not able to speak to you bad or good;
24.51: indeed, Rebekah is before you, take and go, and she is a wife to your lord's son, as Jehovah has spoken.'
24.52: And it comes to pass, when the servant of Abraham has heard their words, that he bows himself toward the earth before Jehovah;
24.53: and the servant takes out vessels of silver, and vessels of gold, and garments, and gives to Rebekah; precious things also he has given to her brother and to her mother.
24.54: And they eat and drink, he and the men who are with him, and lodge all night; and they rise in the morning, and he says, `Send me to my lord;'
24.55: and her brother says--her mother also--`Let the young person abide with us a week or ten days, afterwards does she go.'
24.56: And he says to them, `Do not delay me, seeing Jehovah has prospered my way; send me away, and I go to my lord;'
24.57: and they say, `Let us call for the young person, and ask at her mouth;'
24.58: and they call for Rebekah, and say to her, `Do you go with this man?' and she says, `I go.'
24.59: And they send away Rebekah their sister, and her nurse, and Abraham's servant, and his men;
24.60: and they bless Rebekah, and say to her, `You are our sister; become you thousands of myriads, and your seed does possess the gate of those hating it.'
24.61: And Rebekah and her young women arise, and ride on the camels, and go after the man; and the servant takes Rebekah and goes.
24.62: And Isaac has come in from the entrance of the Well of the Living One, my Beholder; and he is dwelling in the land of the south,
24.63: and Isaac goes out to meditate in the field, at the turning of the evening, and he lifts up his eyes, and looks, and indeed, camels are coming.
24.64: And Rebekah lifts up her eyes, and sees Isaac, and alights from off the camel;
24.65: and she says to the servant, `Who is this man who is walking in the field to meet us?' and the servant says, `It is my lord;' and she takes the veil, and covers herself.
24.66: And the servant recounts to Isaac all the things that he has done,
24.67: and Isaac brings her in to the tent of Sarah his mother, and he takes Rebekah, and she becomes his wife, and he loves her, and Isaac is comforted after the death of his mother.

25.1: And Abraham adds and takes a wife, and her name is Keturah;
25.2: and she bears to him Zimran, and Jokshan, and Medan, and Midian, and Ishbak, and Shuah.
25.3: And Jokshan has begotten Sheba and Dedan; and the sons of Dedan were Asshurim, and Letushim, and Leummim;
25.4: and the sons of Midian are Ephah, and Epher, and Hanoch, and Abidah, and Eldaah: all these are sons of Keturah.
25.5: And Abraham gives all that he has to Isaac;
25.6: and to the sons of the concubines whom Abraham has, Abraham has given gifts, and sends them away from Isaac his son (in his being yet alive) eastward, to the east country.
25.7: And these are the days of the years of the life of Abraham, which he lived, a hundred and seventy and five years;
25.8: and Abraham expires, and dies in a good old age, aged and satisfied, and is gathered to his people.
25.9: And Isaac and Ishmael his sons bury him at the cave of Machpelah, at the field of Ephron, son of Zoar the Hittite, which is before Mamre--
25.10: the field which Abraham bought from the sons of Heth--there has Abraham been buried, and Sarah his wife.
25.11: And it comes to pass after the death of Abraham, that God blesses Isaac his son; and Isaac dwells by the Well of the Living One, my Beholder.
25.12: And these are births of Ishmael, Abraham's son, whom Hagar the Egyptian, Sarah's handmaid, has borne to Abraham;
25.13: and these are the names of the sons of Ishmael, by their names, according to their births: first-born of Ishmael, Nebajoth; and Kedar, and Adbeel, and Mibsam,
25.14: and Mishma, and Dumah, and Massa,
25.15: Hadar, and Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah:
25.16: these are sons of Ishmael, and these their names, by their villages, and by their towers; twelve princes according to their peoples.
25.17: And these are the years of the life of Ishmael, a hundred and thirty and seven years; and he expires, and dies, and is gathered to his people;
25.18: and they tabernacle from Havilah to Shur, which is before Egypt, in your going toward Asshur; in the presence of all his brethren has he fallen.
25.19: And these are births of Isaac, Abraham's son: Abraham has begotten Isaac;
25.20: and Isaac is a son of forty years in his taking Rebekah, daughter of Bethuel the Aramaean, from Padan-Aram, sister of Laban the Aramaean, to him for a wife.
25.21: And Isaac makes entreaty to Jehovah before his wife, for she is barren: and Jehovah is entreated of him, and Rebekah his wife conceives,
25.22: and the children struggle together within her, and she says, `If it is right--why am I thus?' and she goes to seek Jehovah.
25.23: And Jehovah says to her, `Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples from your bowels are parted; and the one people than the other people is stronger; and the elder does serve the younger.'
25.24: And her days to bear are fulfilled, and indeed, twins are in her womb;
25.25: and the first comes out all red as a hairy robe, and they call his name Esau;
25.26: and afterwards has his brother come out, and his hand is taking hold on Esau's heel, and one calls his name Jacob; and Isaac is a son of sixty years in her bearing them.
25.27: And the youths grew, and Esau is a man acquainted with hunting, a man of the field; and Jacob is a plain man, inhabiting tents;
25.28: and Isaac loves Esau, for his hunting is in his mouth; and Rebekah is loving Jacob.
25.29: And Jacob boils pottage, and Esau comes in from the field, and he is weary;
25.30: and Esau says to Jacob, `Let me eat, I pray you, some of this red red thing, for I am weary;' therefore has one called his name Edom Red;
25.31: and Jacob says, `Sell to-day your birthright to me.'
25.32: And Esau says, `Indeed, I am going to die, and what is this to me--birthright?'
25.33: and Jacob says, `Swear to me to-day:' and he swears to him, and sells his birthright to Jacob;
25.34: and Jacob has given to Esau bread and pottage of lentiles, and he eats, and drinks, and rises, and goes; and Esau despises the birthright.

26.1: And there is a famine in the land, besides the first famine which was in the days of Abraham, and Isaac goes to Abimelech king of the Philistines, to Gerar.
26.2: And Jehovah appears to him, and says, `Go not down toward Egypt, tabernacle in the land concerning which I speak to you,
26.3: sojourn in this land, and I am with you, and bless you, for to you and to your seed I give all these lands, and I have established the oath which I have sworn to Abraham your father;
26.4: and I have multiplied your seed as stars of the heavens, and I have given to your seed all these lands; and blessed themselves in your seed have all nations of the earth;
26.5: because that Abraham has hearkened to My voice, and keeps My charge, My commands, My statutes, and My laws.'
26.7: and men of the place ask him of his wife, and he says, `She is my sister:' for he has been afraid to say, `My wife--lest the men of the place kill me for Rebekah, for she is of good appearance.'
26.8: And it comes to pass, when the days have been prolonged to him there, that Abimelech king of the Philistines looks through the window, and sees, and indeed, Isaac is playing with Rebekah his wife.
26.9: And Abimelech calls for Isaac, and says, `Indeed, she is surely your wife; and how have you said, She is my sister?' and Isaac says to him, `Because I said, Lest I die for her.'
26.10: And Abimelech says, `What is this you have done to us? as a little thing one of the people had lain with your wife, and you had brought upon us guilt;'
26.11: and Abimelech commands all the people, saying, `He who comes against this man or against his wife, dying does die.'
26.12: And Isaac sows in that land, and finds in that year a hundredfold, and Jehovah blesses him;
26.13: and the man is great, and goes on, going on and becoming great, till that he has been very great,
26.14: and he has possession of a flock, and possession of a herd, and an abundant service; and the Philistines envy him,
26.15: and all the wells which his father's servants digged in the days of Abraham his father, the Philistines have stopped them, and fill them with dust.
26.16: And Abimelech says to Isaac, `Go from us; for you have become much mightier than we;'
26.17: and Isaac goes from from there, and encamps in the valley of Gerar, and dwells there;
26.18: and Isaac turns back, and digs the wells of water which they digged in the days of Abraham his father, which the Philistines do stop after the death of Abraham, and he calls to them names according to the names which his father called them.
26.19: And Isaac's servants dig in the valley, and find there a well of living water,
26.20: and shepherds of Gerar strive with shepherds of Isaac, saying, `The water is ours;' and he calls the name of the well `Strife,' because they have striven habitually with him;
26.21: and they dig another well, and they strive also for it, and he calls its name `Hatred.'
26.22: And he removes from from there, and digs another well, and they have not striven for it, and he calls its name Enlargements, and says, `For--now has Jehovah given enlargement to us, and we have been fruitful in the land.'
26.23: And he goes up from from there to Beer-Sheba,
26.24: and Jehovah appears to him during that night, and says, `I am the God of Abraham your father, fear not, for I am with you, and have blessed you, and have multiplied your seed, because of Abraham My servant;'
26.25: and he builds there an altar, and preaches in the name of Jehovah, and stretches out there his tent, and there Isaac's servants dig a well.
26.26: And Abimelech has gone to him from Gerar, and Ahuzzath his friend, and Phichol head of his host;
26.27: and Isaac says to them, `Wherefore have you come to me, and you have hated me, and you send me away from you?'
26.28: And they say, `We have certainly seen that Jehovah has been with you, and we say, `Let there be, we pray you, an oath between us, between us and you, and let us make a covenant with you;
26.29: do not evil with us, as we have not touched you, and as we have only done good with you, and send you away in peace; you are now blessed of Jehovah.'
26.30: And he makes for them a banquet, and they eat and drink,
26.31: and rise early in the morning, and swear one to another, and Isaac sends them away, and they go from him in peace.
26.32: And it comes to pass during that day that Isaac's servants come and declare to him concerning the circumstances of the well which they have digged, and say to him, `We have found water;'
26.33: and he calls it Shebah, oath, therefore the name of the city is Beer-Sheba, well of the oath, to this day.
26.34: And Esau is a son of forty years, and he takes a wife, Judith, daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Bashemath, daughter of Elon the Hittite,
26.35: and they are a bitterness of spirit to Isaac and to Rebekah.

27.1: And it comes to pass that Isaac is aged, and his eyes are too dim for seeing, and he calls Esau his elder son, and says to him, `My son;' and he says to him, `Here am I.'
27.2: And he says, `Indeed, I pray you, I have become aged, I have not known the day of my death;
27.3: and now, take up, I pray you, your instruments, your quiver, and your bow, and go out to the field, and hunt for me provision,
27.4: and make for me tasteful things, such as I have loved, and bring in to me, and I do eat, so that my soul does bless you before I die.'
27.5: And Rebekah is hearkening while Isaac is speaking to Esau his son; and Esau goes to the field to hunt provision--to bring in;
27.6: and Rebekah has spoken to Jacob her son, saying, `Indeed, I have heard your father speaking to Esau your brother, saying,
27.7: Bring for me provision, and make for me tasteful things, and I do eat, and bless you before Jehovah before my death.
27.8: `And now, my son, hearken to my voice, to that which I am commanding you:
27.9: Go, I pray you, to the flock, and take for me from from there two good kids of the goats, and I make them tasteful things for your father, such as he has loved;
27.10: and you have taken in to your father, and he has eaten, so that his soul does bless you before his death.
27.11: And Jacob says to Rebekah his mother, `Indeed, Esau my brother is a hairy man, and I a smooth man,
27.12: it may be my father does feel me, and I have been in his eyes as a deceiver, and have brought upon me disesteem, and not a blessing;'
27.13: and his mother says to him, `On me your disesteem, my son; only hearken to my voice, and go, take for me.'
27.14: And he goes, and takes, and brings to his mother, and his mother makes tasteful things, such as his father has loved;
27.15: and Rebekah takes the desirable garments of Esau her elder son, which are with her in the house, and does put on Jacob her younger son;
27.16: and the skins of the kids of the goats she has put on his hands, and on the smooth of his neck,
27.17: and she gives the tasteful things, and the bread which she has made, into the hand of Jacob her son.
27.18: And he comes in to his father, and says, `My father;' and he says, `Here am I; who are you, my son?'
27.19: And Jacob says to his father, `I am Esau your first-born; I have done as you have spoken to me; rise, I pray you, sit, and eat of my provision, so that your soul does bless me.'
27.20: And Isaac says to his son, `What is this you have hasted to find, my son?' and he says, `That which Jehovah your God has caused to come before me.'
27.21: And Isaac says to Jacob, `Come nigh, I pray you, and I feel you, my son, whether you are he, my son Esau, or not.'
27.22: And Jacob comes nigh to Isaac his father, and he feels him, and says, `The voice is the voice of Jacob, and the hands hands of Esau.'
27.23: And he has not discerned him, for his hands have been hairy, as the hands of Esau his brother, and he blesses him,
27.24: and says, `You are he--my son Esau?' and he says, `I am.'
27.25: And he says, `Bring nigh to me, and I do eat of my son's provision, so that my soul does bless you;' and he brings nigh to him, and he eats; and he brings to him wine, and he drinks.
27.26: And Isaac his father says to him, `Come nigh, I pray you, and kiss me, my son;'
27.27: and he comes nigh, and kisses him, and he smells the fragrance of his garments, and blesses him, and says, `See, the fragrance of my son is as the fragrance of a field which Jehovah has blessed;
27.28: and God does give to you of the dew of heaven, and of the fatness of the earth, and abundance of corn and wine;
27.29: peoples serve you, and nations bow themselves to you, be you mighty over your brethren, and the sons of your mother bow themselves to you; those who curse you are cursed, and those who bless you are blessed.'
27.30: And it comes to pass, as Isaac has finished blessing Jacob, and Jacob is only just going out from the presence of Isaac his father, that Esau his brother has come in from his hunting;
27.31: and he also makes tasteful things, and brings to his father, and says to his father, `Let my father arise, and eat of his son's provision, so that your soul does bless me.'
27.32: And Isaac his father says to him, `Who are you?' and he says, `I am your son, your first-born, Esau;'
27.33: and Isaac trembles a very great trembling, and says, `Who, now, is he who has provided provision, and brings in to me, and I eat of all before you come in, and I bless him? --yes, blessed is he.'
27.34: When Esau hears the words of his father, then he cries a very great and bitter cry, and says to his father, `Bless me, me also, O my father;'
27.35: and he says, `Your brother has come with subtilty, and takes your blessing.'
27.36: And he says, `Is it because one called his name Jacob that he does take me by the heel these two times? my birthright he has taken; and indeed, now, he has taken my blessing;' he says also, `Have you not kept back a blessing for me?'
27.37: And Isaac answers and says to Esau, `Indeed, a mighty one have I set him over you, and all his brethren have I given to him for servants, and with corn and wine have I sustained him; and for you now, what shall I do, my son?'
27.38: And Esau says to his father, `One blessing have you my father? bless me, me also, O my father;' and Esau lifts up his voice, and weeps.
27.39: And Isaac his father answers and says to him, `Indeed, of the fatness of the earth is your dwelling, and of the dew of the heavens from above;
27.40: and by your sword do you live, and your brother do you serve; and it has come to pass when you rule, that you have broken his yoke from off your neck.'
27.41: And Esau hates Jacob, because of the blessing with which his father blessed him, and Esau says in his heart, `The days of mourning for my father draw near, and I slay Jacob my brother.'
27.42: And the words of Esau her elder son are declared to Rebekah, and she sends and calls for Jacob her younger son, and says to him, `Indeed, Esau your brother is comforting himself in regard to you--to slay you;
27.43: and now, my son, hearken to my voice, and rise, flee for yourself to Laban my brother, to Haran,
27.44: and you have dwelt with him some days, till your brother's fury turn back,
27.45: till your brother's anger turn back from you, and he has forgotten that which you have done to him, and I have sent and taken you from from there; why am I bereaved even of you both the same day?'
27.46: And Rebekah says to Isaac, `I have been disgusted with my life because of the presence of the daughters of Heth; if Jacob take a wife of the daughters of Heth, like these--from the daughters of the land--why do I live?'

28.1: And Isaac calls to Jacob, and blesses him, and commands him, and says to him, `You do not take a wife of the daughters of Caanan;
28.2: rise, go to Padan-Aram, to the house of Bethuel, your mother's father, and take for yourself from from there a wife, of the daughters of Laban, your mother's brother;
28.3: and God Almighty does bless you, and make you fruitful, and multiply you, and you have become an assembly of peoples;
28.4: and He does give to you the blessing of Abraham, to you and to your seed with you, to cause you to possess the land of your sojournings, which God gave to Abraham.'
28.5: And Isaac sends away Jacob, and he goes to Padan-Aram, to Laban, son of Bethuel the Aramaean, brother of Rebekah, mother of Jacob and Esau.
28.6: And Esau sees that Isaac has blessed Jacob, and has sent him to Padan-Aram to take to himself from from there a wife--in his blessing him that he lays a charge upon him, saying, You do not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan--
28.7: that Jacob hearkens to his father and to his mother, and goes to Padan-Aram--
28.8: and Esau sees that the daughters of Canaan are evil in the eyes of Isaac his father,
28.9: and Esau goes to Ishmael, and takes Mahalath, daughter of Ishmael, Abraham's son, sister of Nebajoth, to his wives, to himself, for a wife.
28.10: And Jacob goes out from Beer-Sheba, and goes toward Haran,
28.11: and he touches at a certain place, and lodges there, for the sun has gone in, and he takes of the stones of the place, and makes them his pillows, and lies down in that place.
28.12: And he dreams, and indeed, a ladder set up on the earth, and its head is touching the heavens; and indeed, messengers of God are going up and coming down by it;
28.13: and indeed, Jehovah is standing upon it, and He says, `I am Jehovah, God of Abraham your father, and God of Isaac; the land on which you are lying, to you I give it, and to your seed;
28.14: and your seed has been as the dust of the land, and you have broken forth westward, and eastward, and northward, and southward, and all families of the ground have been blessed in you and in your seed.
28.15: `And indeed, I am with you, and have kept you wherever you go, and have caused you to turn back to this ground; for I leave you not till that I have surely done that which I have spoken to you.'
28.16: And Jacob awakes out of his sleep, and says, `Surely Jehovah is in this place, and I knew not;'
28.17: and he fears, and says, `How fearful is this place; this is nothing but a house of God, and this a gate of the heavens.'
28.18: And Jacob rises early in the morning, and takes the stone which he has made his pillows, and makes it a standing pillar, and pours oil upon its top,
28.19: and he calls the name of that place Bethel, house of God, and yet, Luz is the name of the city at the first.
28.20: And Jacob vows a vow, saying, `Seeing God is with me, and has kept me in this way which I am going, and has given to me bread to eat, and a garment to put on--
28.21: when I have turned back in peace to the house of my father, and Jehovah has become my God,
28.22: then this stone which I have made a standing pillar is a house of God, and all that You do give to me--tithing I tithe to You.'

29.1: And Jacob lifts up his feet, and goes toward the land of the sons of the east;
29.2: and he looks, and indeed, a well in the field, and indeed, there three droves of a flock crouching by it, for from that well they water the droves, and the great stone is on the mouth of the well.
29.3: (When there have all the droves been gathered, and they have rolled the stone from off the mouth of the well, and have watered the flock, then they have turned back the stone on the mouth of the well to its place.)
29.4: And Jacob says to them, `My brethren, from from where are you?' and they say, `We are from Haran.'
29.5: And he says to them, `Have you known Laban, son of Nahor?' and they say, `We have known.'
29.6: And he says to them, `Has he peace?' and they say, `Peace; and indeed, Rachel his daughter is coming with the flock.'
29.7: And he says, `Indeed, the day is still great, it is not time for the cattle to be gathered; water you the flock, and go, delight yourselves.'
29.8: And they say, `We are not able, till that all the droves be gathered together, and they have rolled away the stone from the mouth of the well, and we have watered the flock.'
29.9: He is yet speaking with them, and Rachel has come with the flock which her father has, for she is shepherdess;
29.10: and it comes to pass when Jacob has seen Rachel, daughter of Laban his mother's brother, and the flock of Laban his mother's brother, that Jacob comes nigh and rolls the stone from off the mouth of the well, and waters the flock of Laban his mother's brother.
29.11: And Jacob kisses Rachel, and lifts up his voice, and weeps,
29.12: and Jacob declares to Rachel that he is her father's brother, and that he is Rebekah's son, and she runs and declares to her father.
29.13: And it comes to pass, when Laban hears the report of Jacob his sister's son, that he runs to meet him, and embraces him, and kisses him, and brings him in to his house; and he recounts to Laban all these things,
29.14: and Laban says to him, `Only my bone and my flesh are you;' and he dwells with him a month of days.
29.15: And Laban says to Jacob, `Is it because you are my brother that you have served me for nought? declare to me what is your hire.'
29.16: And Laban has two daughters, the name of the elder is Leah, and the name of the younger Rachel,
29.17: and the eyes of Leah are tender, and Rachel has been fair of form and fair of appearance.
29.18: And Jacob loves Rachel, and says, `I serve you seven years for Rachel your younger daughter:'
29.19: and Laban says, `It is better for me to give her to you than to give her to another man; dwell with me;'
29.20: and Jacob serves for Rachel seven years; and they are in his eyes as some days, because of his loving her.
29.21: And Jacob says to Laban, `Give up my wife, for my days have been fulfilled, and I go in to her;'
29.22: and Laban gathers all the men of the place, and makes a banquet.
29.23: And it comes to pass in the evening, that he takes Leah, his daughter, and brings her in to him, and he goes in to her;
29.24: and Laban gives to her Zilpah, his maid-servant, to Leah his daughter, a maid-servant.
29.25: And it comes to pass in the morning, that indeed, it is Leah; and he says to Laban, `What is this you have done to me? for Rachel have I not served with you? and why have you deceived me?'
29.26: And Laban says, `It is not done so in our place, to give the younger before the first-born;
29.27: fulfil the week of this one, and we give to you also this one, for the service which you do serve with me yet seven other years.'
29.28: And Jacob does so, and fulfils the week of this one, and he gives to him Rachel his daughter, to him for a wife;
29.29: and Laban gives to Rachel his daughter Bilhah his maid-servant, for a maid-servant to her.
29.30: And he goes in also to Rachel, and he also loves Rachel more than Leah; and he serves with him yet seven other years.
29.31: And Jehovah sees that Leah is the hated one, and He opens her womb, and Rachel is barren;
29.32: and Leah conceives, and bears a son, and calls his name Reuben, for she said, `Because Jehovah has looked on my affliction; because now does my husband love me.'
29.33: And she conceives again, and bears a son, and says, `Because Jehovah has heard that I am the hated one, He also gives to me even this one;' and she calls his name Simeon.
29.34: And she conceives again, and bears a son, and says, `Now is the time, my husband is joined to me, because I have born to him three sons,' therefore has one called his name Levi.
29.35: And she conceives again, and bears a son, and says this time, `I praise Jehovah;' therefore has she called his name Judah; and she ceases from bearing.

30.1: And Rachel sees that she has not borne to Jacob, and Rachel is envious of her sister, and says to Jacob, `Give me sons, and if there is none--I die.'
30.2: And Jacob's anger burns against Rachel, and he says, `Am I in stead of God who has withheld from you the fruit of the womb?'
30.3: And she says, `Indeed, my handmaid Bilhah, go in to her, and she does bear on my knees, and I am built up, even I, from her;'
30.4: and she gives to him Bilhah her maid-servant for a wife, and Jacob goes in to her;
30.5: and Bilhah conceives, and bears to Jacob a son,
30.6: and Rachel says, `God has decided for me, and also has hearkened to my voice, and gives to me a son;' therefore has she called his name Dan.
30.7: And Bilhah, Rachel's maid-servant, conceives again, and bears a second son to Jacob,
30.8: and Rachel says, `With wrestlings of God I have wrestled with my sister, yes, I have prevailed;' and she calls his name Napthali.
30.9: And Leah sees that she has ceased from bearing, and she takes Zilpah her maid-servant, and gives her to Jacob for a wife;
30.10: and Zilpah, Leah's maid-servant, bears to Jacob a son,
30.11: and Leah says, `A troop is coming;' and she calls his name Gad.
30.12: And Zilpah, Leah's maid-servant, bears a second son to Jacob,
30.13: and Leah says, `Because of my happiness, for daughters have pronounced me happy;' and she calls his name Asher.
30.14: And Reuben goes in the days of wheat-harvest, and finds love-apples in the field, and brings them in to Leah, his mother, and Rachel says to Leah, `Give to me, I pray you, of the love-apples of your son.'
30.15: And she says to her, `Is your taking my husband a little thing, that you have taken also the love-apples of my son?' and Rachel says, `Therefore does he lie with you to-night, for your son's love-apples.'
30.16: And Jacob comes in from the field at evening; and Leah goes to meet him, and says, `To me do you come in, for hiring I have hired you with my son's love-apples;' and he lies with her during that night.
30.17: And God hearkens to Leah, and she conceives, and bears to Jacob a son, a fifth,
30.18: and Leah says, `God has given my hire, because I have given my maid-servant to my husband;' and she calls his name Issachar.
30.19: And conceive again does Leah, and she bears a sixth son to Jacob,
30.20: and Leah says, `God has endowed me--a good dowry; this time does my husband dwell with me, for I have borne to him six sons;' and she calls his name Zebulun;
30.21: and afterwards has she born a daughter, and calls her name Dinah.
30.22: And God remembers Rachel, and God hearkens to her, and opens her womb,
30.23: and she conceives and bears a son, and says, `God has gathered up my reproach;'
30.24: and she calls his name Joseph, saying, `Jehovah is adding to me another son.'
30.25: And it comes to pass, when Rachel has borne Joseph, that Jacob says to Laban, `Send me away, and I go to my place, and to my land;
30.26: give up my wives and my children, for whom I have served you, and I go; for you--you have known my service which I have served you.'
30.27: And Laban says to him, `If, I pray you, I have found grace in your eyes--I have observed diligently that Jehovah does bless me for your sake.'
30.28: He says also, `Define your hire to me, and I give.'
30.29: And he says to him, `You--you have known that which I have served you in, and that which your substance was with me;
30.30: for it is little which you have had at my appearance, and it breaks forth into a multitude, and Jehovah blesses you at my coming; and now, when do I make, I also, for my own house?'
30.31: And he says, `What do I give to you?' And Jacob says, `You do not give me anything; if you do for me this thing, I turn back; I have delight; your flock I watch;
30.32: I pass through all your flock to-day to turn aside from from there every sheep speckled and spotted, and every brown sheep among the lambs, and speckled and spotted among the goats--and it has been my hire;
30.33: and my righteousness has answered for me in the day to come, when it comes in for my hire before your face; --every one which is not speckled and spotted among my goats, and brown among my lambs--it is stolen with me.'
30.34: And Laban says, `Indeed, O that it were according to your word;'
30.35: and he turns aside during that day the ring-streaked and the spotted he-goats, and all the speckled and the spotted she-goats, every one that has white in it, and every brown one among the lambs, and he gives into the hand of his sons,
30.36: and sets a journey of three days between himself and Jacob; and Jacob is feeding the rest of the flock of Laban.
30.37: And Jacob takes to himself a rod of fresh poplar, and of the hazel and chesnut, and does peel in them white peelings, making bare the white that is on the rods,
30.38: and sets up the rods which he has peeled in the gutters in the watering troughs (when the flock comes in to drink), over-against the flock, that they may conceive in their coming in to drink;
30.39: and the flocks conceive at the rods, and the flock bears ring-streaked, speckled, and spotted ones.
30.40: And the lambs has Jacob parted, and he puts the face of the flock toward the ring-streaked, also all the brown in the flock of Laban, and he sets his own droves by themselves, and has not set them near Laban's flock.
30.41: And it has come to pass whenever the strong ones of the flock conceive, that Jacob set the rods before the eyes of the flock in the gutters, to cause them to conceive by the rods,
30.42: and when the flock is feeble, he does not set them; and the feeble ones have been Laban's, and the strong ones Jacob's.
30.43: And the man increases very exceedingly, and has many flocks, and maid-servants, and men-servants, and camels, and asses.

31.1: And he hears the words of Laban's sons, saying, `Jacob has taken all that our father has; yes, from that which our father has, he has made all this honour;'
31.2: and Jacob sees the face of Laban, and indeed, it is not with him as heretofore.
31.3: And Jehovah says to Jacob, `Turn back to the land of your fathers, and to your kindred, and I am with you.'
31.4: And Jacob sends and calls for Rachel and for Leah to the field to his flock;
31.5: and says to them, `I am beholding your father's face--that it is not toward me as heretofore, and the God of my father has been with me,
31.6: and you--you have known that with all my power I have served your father,
31.7: and your father has played upon me, and has changed my hire ten times; and God has not suffered him to do evil with me.
31.8: `If he say thus: The speckled are your hire, then bare all the flock speckled ones; and if he say thus: The ring-streaked are your hire, then bare all the flock ring-streaked;
31.9: and God takes away the substance of your father, and does give to me.
31.10: `And it comes to pass at the time of the flock conceiving, that I lift up my eyes and see in a dream, and indeed, the he-goats, which are going up on the flock, are ring-streaked, speckled, and grisled;
31.11: and the messenger of God says to me in the dream, Jacob, and I say, Here am I.
31.12: `And He says, Lift up, I pray you, your eyes, and see--all the he-goats which are going up on the flock are ring-streaked, speckled, and grisled, for I have seen all that Laban is doing to you;
31.13: I am the God of Bethel where you have anointed a standing pillar, where you have vowed a vow to me; now, arise, go out from this land, and turn back to the land of your birth.'
31.14: And Rachel answers--Leah also--and says to him, `Have we yet a portion and inheritance in the house of our father?
31.15: have we not been reckoned strangers to him? for he has sold us, and he also utterly consumes our money;
31.16: for all the wealth which God has taken away from our father, it is ours, and our children's; and now, all that God has said to you--do.'
31.17: And Jacob rises, and lifts up his sons and his wives on the camels,
31.18: and leads all his cattle, and all his substance which he has acquired, the cattle of his getting, which he has acquired in Padan-Aram, to go to Isaac his father, to the land of Canaan.
31.19: And Laban has gone to shear his flock, and Rachel steals the teraphim which her father has;
31.20: and Jacob deceives the heart of Laban the Aramaean, because he has not declared to him that he is fleeing;
31.21: and he flees, he and all that he has, and rises, and passes over the River, and sets his face toward the mount of Gilead.
31.22: And it is told to Laban on the third day that Jacob has fled,
31.23: and he takes his brethren with him, and pursues after him a journey of seven days, and overtakes him in the mount of Gilead.
31.24: And God comes in to Laban the Aramaean in a dream of the night, and says to him, `Take heed to yourself lest you speak with Jacob from good to evil.'
31.25: And Laban overtakes Jacob; and Jacob has fixed his tent in the mount; and Laban with his brethren have fixed theirs in the mount of Gilead.
31.26: And Laban says to Jacob, `What have you done that you do deceive my heart, and lead away my daughters as captives of the sword?
31.27: Why have you hidden yourself to flee, and deceive me, and have not declared to me, and I send you away with joy and with songs, with tabret and with harp,
31.28: and have not suffered me to kiss my sons and my daughters? --now you have acted foolishly in doing so;
31.29: my hand is to God to do evil with you, but the God of your father yesternight has spoken to me, saying, Take heed to yourself from speaking with Jacob from good to evil.
31.30: `And now, you have certainly gone, because you have been very desirous for the house of your father; why have you stolen my gods?'
31.31: And Jacob answers and says to Laban, `Because I was afraid, for I said, Lest you take violently away your daughters from me;
31.32: with whomever you find your gods--he does not live; before our brethren discern for yourself what is with me, and take to yourself:' and Jacob has not known that Rachel has stolen them.
31.33: And Laban goes into the tent of Jacob, and into the tent of Leah, and into the tent of the two handmaidens, and has not found; and he goes out from the tent of Leah, and goes into the tent of Rachel.
31.34: And Rachel has taken the teraphim, and puts them in the furniture of the camel, and sits upon them; and Laban feels all the tent, and has not found;
31.35: and she says to her father, `Let it not be displeasing in the eyes of my lord that I am not able to rise at your presence, for the way of women is on me;' and he searches, and has not found the teraphim.
31.36: And it is displeasing to Jacob, and he strives with Laban; and Jacob answers and says to Laban, `What is my transgression? what my sin, that you have burned after me?
31.37: for you have felt all my vessels: what have you found of all the vessels of your house? set here before my brethren, and your brethren, and they decide between us both.
31.38: `These twenty years I am with you: your ewes and your she-goats have not miscarried, and the rams of your flock I have not eaten;
31.39: the torn I have not brought in to you--I, I repay it--from my hand you do seek it; I have been deceived by day, and I have been deceived by night;
31.40: I have been thus: in the day consumed me has drought, and frost by night, and wander does my sleep from my eyes.
31.41: `This is to me twenty years in your house: I have served you fourteen years for your two daughters, and six years for your flock; and you change my hire ten times;
31.42: unless the God of my father, the God of Abraham, and the Fear of Isaac, had been for me, surely now empty you had sent me away; my affliction and the labour of my hands has God seen, and reproves yesternight.'
31.43: And Laban answers and says to Jacob, `The daughters are my daughters, and the sons my sons, and the flock my flock, and all that you are seeing is mine; and to my daughters--what do I to these to-day, or to their sons whom they have born?
31.44: and now, come, let us make a covenant, I and you, and it has been for a witness between me and you.'
31.45: And Jacob takes a stone, and lifts it up for a standing pillar;
31.46: and Jacob says to his brethren, `Gather stones,' and they take stones, and make a heap; and they eat there on the heap;
31.47: and Laban calls it Jegar-Sahadutha; and Jacob has called it Galeed.
31.48: And Laban says, `This heap is witness between me and you to-day;' therefore has he called its name Galeed;
31.49: Mizpah also, for he said, `Jehovah does watch between me and you, for we are hidden one from another;
31.50: if you afflict my daughters, or take wives beside my daughters--there is no man with us--see, God is witness between me and you.'
31.51: And Laban says to Jacob, `Indeed, this heap, and indeed, the standing pillar which I have cast between me and you;
31.52: this heap is witness, and the standing pillar is witness, that I do not pass over this heap to you, and that you do not pass over this heap and this standing pillar to me--for evil;
31.53: the God of Abraham and the God of Nahor, does judge between us--the God of their father,' and Jacob swears by the Fear of his father Isaac.
31.54: And Jacob sacrifices a sacrifice in the mount, and calls to his brethren to eat bread, and they eat bread, and lodge in the mount;
31.55: and Laban rises early in the morning, and kisses his sons and his daughters, and blesses them; and Laban goes on, and turns back to his place.

32.1: And Jacob has gone on his way, and messengers of God come upon him;
32.2: and Jacob says, when he has seen them, `This is the camp of God;' and he calls the name of that place `Two Camps.'
32.3: And Jacob sends messengers before him to Esau his brother, toward the land of Seir, the field of Edom,
32.4: and commands them, saying, `Thus do you say to my lord, to Esau: Thus said your servant Jacob, With Laban I have sojourned, and I tarry until now;
32.5: and I have ox, and ass, flock, and man-servant, and maid-servant, and I send to declare to my lord, to find grace in his eyes.'
32.6: And the messengers turn back to Jacob, saying, `We came in to your brother, to Esau, and he also is coming to meet you, and four hundred men with him;'
32.7: and Jacob fears exceedingly, and is distressed, and he divides the people who are with him, and the flock, and the herd, and the camels, into two camps,
32.8: and says, `If Esau come in to the one camp, and have smitten it--then the camp which is left has been for an escape.'
32.9: And Jacob says, `God of my father Abraham, and God of my father Isaac, Jehovah who says to me, Turn back to your land, and to your kindred, and I do good with you:
32.10: I have been unworthy of all the kind acts, and of all the truth which You have done with your servant--for, with my staff I passed over this Jordan, and now I have become two camps.
32.11: `Deliver me, I pray You, from the hand of my brother, from the hand of Esau: for I am fearing him, less he come and have smitten me--mother beside sons;
32.12: and You--You have said, I certainly do good with you, and have set your seed as the sand of the sea, which is not numbered because of the multitude.'
32.13: And he lodges there during that night, and takes from that which is coming into his hand, a present for Esau his brother:
32.14: she-goats two hundred, and he-goats twenty, ewes two hundred, and rams twenty,
32.15: suckling camels and their young ones thirty, cows forty, and bullocks ten, she-asses twenty, and foals ten;
32.16: and he gives into the hand of his servants, every drove by itself, and says to his servants, `Pass over before me, and a space you do put between drove and drove.'
32.17: And he commands the first, saying, `When Esau my brother meets you, and has asked you, saying, Whose are you? and where do you go? and whose are these before you?
32.18: then you have said, Your servant Jacob's: it is a present sent to my lord, to Esau; and indeed, he also is behind us.'
32.19: And he commands also the second, also the third, also all who are going after the droves, saying, `According to this manner do you speak to Esau in your finding him,
32.20: and you have said also, Indeed, your servant Jacob is behind us;' for he said, `I pacify his face with the present which is going before me, and afterwards I see his face; it may be he lifts up my face;'
32.21: and the present passes over before his face, and he has lodged during that night in the camp.
32.22: And he rises in that night, and takes his two wives, and his two maid-servants, and his eleven children, and passes over the passage of Jabbok;
32.23: and he takes them, and causes them to pass over the brook, and he causes that which he has to pass over.
32.24: And Jacob is left alone, and one wrestles with him till the ascending of the dawn;
32.25: and he sees that he is not able for him, and he comes against the hollow of his thigh, and the hollow of Jacob's thigh is disjointed in his wrestling with him;
32.26: and he says, `Send me away, for the dawn has ascended:' and he says, `I send you not away, except you have blessed me.'
32.27: And he says to him, `What is your name?' and he says, `Jacob.'
32.28: And he says, `Your name is no more called Jacob, but Israel; for you have been a prince with God and with men, and do prevail.'
32.29: And Jacob asks, and says, `Declare, I pray you, your name;' and he says, `Why is this, you ask for My name?' and He blesses him there.
32.30: And Jacob calls the name of the place Peniel: for `I have seen God face to face, and my life is delivered;'
32.31: and the sun rises on him when he has passed over Penuel, and he is halting on his thigh;
32.32: therefore the sons of Israel do not eat the sinew which shrank, which is on the hollow of the thigh, to this day, because He came against the hollow of Jacob's thigh, against the sinew which shrank.

33.1: And Jacob lifts up his eyes, and looks, and indeed, Esau is coming, and with him four hundred men; and he divides the children to Leah, and to Rachel, and to the two maid-servants;
33.2: and he sets the maid-servants and their children first, and Leah and her children behind, and Rachel and Joseph last.
33.3: And he himself passed over before them, and bows himself to the earth seven times, until his drawing nigh to his brother,
33.4: and Esau runs to meet him, and embraces him, and falls on his neck, and kisses him, and they weep;
33.5: and he lifts up his eyes, and sees the women and the children, and says, `What are these to you?' And he says, `The children with whom God has favoured your servant.'
33.6: And the maid-servants draw nigh, they and their children, and bow themselves;
33.7: and Leah also draws nigh, and her children, and they bow themselves; and afterwards Joseph has drawn nigh with Rachel, and they bow themselves.
33.8: And he says, `What to you is all this camp which I have met?' and he says, `To find grace in the eyes of my lord.'
33.9: And Esau says, `I have abundance, my brother, let it be to yourself that which you have.'
33.10: And Jacob says, `No, I pray you, if, I pray you, I have found grace in your eyes, then you have received my present from my hand, because that I have seen your face, as the seeing of the face of God, and you are pleased with me;
33.11: receive, I pray you, my blessing, which is brought to you, because God has favoured me, and because I have all things;' and he presses on him, and he receives,
33.12: and says, `Let us journey and go on, and I go on before you.'
33.13: And he says to him, `My lord knows that the children are tender, and the suckling flock and the herd are with me; when they have beaten them one day, then has all the flock died.
33.14: Let my lord, I pray you, pass over before his servant, and I--I lead on gently, according to the foot of the work which is before me, and to the foot of the children, until that I come to my lord, to Seir.'
33.15: And Esau says, `Let me, I pray you, place with you some of the people who are with me;' and he said, `Why is this? I find grace in the eyes of my lord.'
33.16: And turn back on that day does Esau on his way to Seir;
33.17: and Jacob has journeyed to Succoth, and builds to himself a house, and for his cattle has made booths, therefore has he called the name of the place Succoth.
33.18: And Jacob comes in to Shalem, a city of Shechem, which is in the land of Canaan, in his coming from Padan-Aram, and encamps before the city,
33.19: and he buys the portion of the field where he has stretched out his tent, from the hand of the sons of Hamor, father of Shechem, for a hundred kesitah;
33.20: and he sets up there an altar, and proclaims at it God--the God of Israel.

34.1: And Dinah, daughter of Leah, whom she has borne to Jacob, goes out to look on the daughters of the land,
34.2: and Shechem, son of Hamor the Hivite, a prince of the land, sees her, and takes her, and lies with her, and humbles her;
34.3: and his soul cleaves to Dinah, daughter of Jacob, and he loves the young person, and speaks to the heart of the young person.
34.4: And Shechem speaks to Hamor his father, saying, `Take for me this damsel for a wife.'
34.5: And Jacob has heard that he has defiled Dinah his daughter, and his sons were with his cattle in the field, and Jacob kept silent till their coming.
34.6: And Hamor, father of Shechem, goes out to Jacob to speak with him;
34.7: and the sons of Jacob came in from the field when they heard, and the men grieve themselves, and it is very displeasing to them, for folly he has done against Israel, to lie with the daughter of Jacob--and so it is not done.
34.8: And Hamor speaks with them, saying, `Shechem, my son, his soul has cleaved to your daughter; give her, I pray you, to him for a wife,
34.9: and join you in marriage with us; your daughters you give to us, and our daughters you take to yourselves,
34.10: and with us you dwell, and the land is before you; dwell you and trade in it, and have possessions in it.'
34.11: And Shechem says to her father, and to her brethren, `Let me find grace in your eyes, and that which you say to me, I give;
34.12: multiply on me exceedingly dowry and gift, and I give as you say to me, and give to me the young person for a wife.'
34.13: And the sons of Jacob answer Shechem and Hamor his father deceitfully, and they speak (because he defiled Dinah their sister),
34.14: and say to them, `We are not able to do this thing, to give our sister to one who has a foreskin: for it is a reproach to us.
34.15: `Only for this we consent to you; if you be as we, to have every male of you circumcised,
34.16: then we have given our daughters to you, and your daughters we take to ourselves, and we have dwelt with you, and have become one people;
34.17: and if you hearken not to us to be circumcised, then we have taken our daughter, and have gone.'
34.18: And their words are good in the eyes of Hamor, and in the eyes of Shechem, Hamor's son;
34.19: and the young man delayed not to do the thing, for he had delight in Jacob's daughter, and he is honourable above all the house of his father.
34.20: And Hamor comes--Shechem his son also--to the gate of their city, and they speak to the men of their city, saying,
34.21: `These men are peaceable with us; then let them dwell in the land, and trade in it; and the land, indeed, is wide before them; their daughters let us take to ourselves for wives, and our daughters give to them.
34.22: `Only for this do the men consent to us, to dwell with us, to become one people, in every male of us being circumcised, as they are circumcised;
34.23: their cattle, and their substance, and all their beasts--are they not ours? only let us consent to them, and they dwell with us.'
34.24: And to Hamor, and to Shechem his son, hearken do all those going out of the gate of his city, and every male is circumcised, all those going out of the gate of his city.
34.25: And it comes to pass, on the third day, in their being pained, that two of the sons of Jacob, Simeon and Levi, Dinah's brethren, take each his sword, and come in against the city confidently, and slay every male;
34.26: and Hamor, and Shechem his son, they have slain by the mouth of the sword, and they take Dinah out of Shechem's house, and go out.
34.27: Jacob's sons have come in upon the wounded, and they spoil the city, because they had defiled their sister;
34.28: their flock and their herd, and their asses, and that which is in the city, and that which is in the field, have they taken;
34.29: and all their wealth, and all their infants, and their wives they have taken captive, and they spoil also all that is in the house.
34.30: And Jacob says to Simeon and to Levi, `You have troubled me, by causing me to stink among the inhabitants of the land, among the Canaanite, and among the Perizzite: and I am few in number, and they have been gathered against me, and have smitten me, and I have been destroyed, I and my house.'
34.31: And they say, `As a harlot does he make our sister?'

35.1: And God says to Jacob, `Rise, go up to Bethel, and dwell there, and make there an altar to God, who appeared to you in your fleeing from the face of Esau your brother.'
35.2: And Jacob says to his household, and to all who are with him, `Turn aside the gods of the stranger which are in your midst, and cleanse yourselves, and change your garments;
35.3: and we rise, and go up to Bethel, and I make there an altar to God, who is answering me in the day of my distress, and is with me in the way that I have gone.'
35.4: And they give to Jacob all the gods of the stranger that are in their hand, and the rings that are in their ears, and Jacob hides them under the oak which is by Shechem;
35.5: and they journey, and the terror of God is on the cities which are round about them, and they have not pursued after the sons of Jacob.
35.6: And Jacob comes in to Luz which is in the land of Canaan (it is Bethel), he and all the people who are with him,
35.7: and he builds there an altar, and proclaims at the place the God of Bethel: for there had God been revealed to him, in his fleeing from the face of his brother.
35.8: And Deborah, Rebekah's nurse, dies, and she is buried at the lower part of Bethel, under the oak, and he calls its name `Oak of weeping.'
35.9: And God appears to Jacob again, in his coming from Padan-Aram, and blesses him;
35.10: and God says to him, `Your name is Jacob: your name is no more called Jacob, but Israel is your name;' and He calls his name Israel.
35.11: And God says to him, `I am God Almighty; be fruitful and multiply, a nation and an assembly of nations is from you, and kings from your loins go out;
35.12: and the land which I have given to Abraham and to Isaac--to you I give it, yes to your seed after you I give the land.'
35.13: And God goes up from him, in the place where He has spoken with him.
35.14: And Jacob sets up a standing pillar in the place where He has spoken with him, a standing pillar of stone, and he pours on it an oblation, and he pours on it oil;
35.15: and Jacob calls the name of the place where God spoke with him Bethel.
35.16: And they journey from Bethel, and there is yet a kibrath of land before entering Ephratha, and Rachel bears, and is sharply pained in her bearing;
35.17: and it comes to pass, in her being sharply pained in her bearing, that the midwife says to her, `Fear not, for this also is a son for you.'
35.18: And it comes to pass in the going out of her soul (for she died), that she calls his name Ben-Oni; and his father called him Benjamin;
35.19: and Rachel dies, and is buried in the way to Ephratha, which is Bethlehem,
35.20: and Jacob sets up a standing pillar over her grave; which is the standing pillar of Rachel's grave to this day.
35.21: And Israel journeys, and stretches out his tent beyond the tower of Edar;
35.22: and it comes to pass in Israel's dwelling in that land, that Reuben goes, and lies with Bilhah his father's concubine; and Israel hears.
35.23: And the sons of Jacob are twelve. Sons of Leah: Jacob's first-born Reuben, and Simeon, and Levi, and Judah, and Issachar, and Zebulun.
35.24: Sons of Rachel: Joseph and Benjamin.
35.25: And sons of Bilhah, Rachel's maid-servant: Dan and Naphtali.
35.26: And sons of Zilpah, Leah's maid-servant: Gad and Asher. These are sons of Jacob, who have been born to him in Padan-Aram.
35.27: And Jacob comes to Isaac his father, at Mamre, the city of Arba (which is Hebron), where Abraham and Isaac have sojourned.
35.28: And the days of Isaac are a hundred and eighty years,
35.29: and Isaac expires, and dies, and is gathered to his people, aged and satisfied with days; and bury him do Esau and Jacob his sons.

36.1: And these are births of Esau, who is Edom.
36.2: Esau has taken his wives from the daughters of Canaan: Adah daughter of Elon the Hittite, and Aholibamah daughter of Anah, daughter of Zibeon the Hivite,
36.3: and Bashemath daughter of Ishmael, sister of Nebajoth.
36.4: And Adah bears to Esau, Eliphaz; and Bashemath has born Reuel;
36.5: and Aholibamah has born Jeush, and Jaalam, and Korah. These are sons of Esau, who were born to him in the land of Canaan.
36.6: And Esau takes his wives, and his sons, and his daughters, and all the persons of his house, and his cattle, and all his beasts, and all his substance which he has acquired in the land of Canaan, and goes into the country from the face of Jacob his brother;
36.7: for their substance was more abundant than to dwell together, and the land of their sojournings was not able to bear them because of their cattle;
36.8: and Esau dwells in mount Seir: Esau is Edom.
36.9: And these are births of Esau, father of Edom, in mount Seir.
36.10: These are the names of the sons of Esau: Eliphaz son of Adah, wife of Esau; Reuel son of Bashemath, wife of Esau.
36.11: And the sons of Eliphaz are Teman, Omar, Zepho, and Gatam, and Kenaz;
36.12: and Timnath has been concubine to Eliphaz son of Esau, and she bears to Eliphaz, Amalek; these are sons of Adah wife of Esau.
36.13: And these are sons of Reuel: Nahath and Zerah, Shammah and Mizzah; these were sons of Bashemath wife of Esau.
36.14: And these have been the sons of Aholibamah daughter of Anah, daughter of Zibeon, wife of Esau; and she bears to Esau, Jeush and Jaalam and Korah.
36.15: These are chiefs of the sons of Esau: sons of Eliphaz, first-born of Esau: chief Teman, chief Omar, chief Zepho, chief Kenaz,
36.16: chief Korah, chief Gatam, chief Amalek; these are chiefs of Eliphaz, in the land of Edom; these are sons of Adah.
36.17: And these are sons of Reuel son of Esau: chief Nahath, chief Zerah, chief Shammah, chief Mizzah; these are chiefs of Reuel, in the land of Edom; these are sons of Bashemath wife of Esau.
36.18: And these are sons of Aholibamah wife of Esau: chief Jeush, chief Jaalam, chief Korah; these are chiefs of Aholibamah daughter of Anah, wife of Esau.
36.19: These are sons of Esau (who is Edom), and these their chiefs.
36.20: These are sons of Seir the Horite, the inhabitants of the land: Lotan, and Shobal, and Zibeon, and Anah,
36.21: and Dishon, and Ezer, and Dishan; these are chiefs of the Horites, sons of Seir, in the land of Edom.
36.22: And the sons of Lotan are Hori and Heman; and a sister of Lotan is Timna.
36.23: And these are sons of Shobal: Alvan and Manahath, and Ebal, Shepho and Onam.
36.24: And these are sons of Zibeon, both Ajah and Anah: it is Anah that has found the Imim in the wilderness, in his feeding the asses of Zibeon his father.
36.25: And these are sons of Anah: Dishon, and Aholibamah daughter of Anah.
36.26: And these are sons of Dishon: Hemdan, and Eshban, and Ithran, and Cheran.
36.27: These are sons of Ezer: Bilhan, and Zaavan, and Akan.
36.28: These are sons of Dishan: Uz and Aran.
36.29: These are chiefs of the Horite: chief Lotan, chief Shobal, chief Zibeon, chief Anah,
36.30: chief Dishon, chief Ezer, chief Dishan: these are chiefs of the Horite in reference to their chiefs in the land of Seir.
36.31: And these are the kings who have reigned in the land of Edom before the reigning of a king over the sons of Israel.
36.32: And Bela son of Beor reigns in Edom, and the name of his city is Dinhabah;
36.33: and Bela dies, and reign in his stead does Jobab son of Zerah from Bozrah;
36.34: and Jobab dies, and reign in his stead does Husham from the land of the Temanite.
36.35: And Husham dies, and reign in his stead does Hadad son of Bedad (who smites Midian in the field of Moab), and the name of his city is Avith;
36.36: and Hadad dies, and reign in his stead does Samlah of Masrekah;
36.37: and Samlah dies, and reign in his stead does Saul from Rehoboth of the River;
36.38: and Saul dies, and reign in his stead does Baal-hanan son of Achbor;
36.39: and Baal-hanan son of Achbor dies, and reign in his stead does Hadar, and the name of his city is Pau; and his wife's name is Mehetabel daughter of Matred, daughter of Me-zahab.
36.40: And these are the names of the chiefs of Esau, according to their families, according to their places, by their names: chief Timnah, chief Alvah, chief Jetheth,
36.41: chief Aholibamah, chief Elah, chief Pinon,
36.42: chief Kenaz, chief Teman, chief Mibzar,
36.43: chief Magdiel, chief Iram: these are chiefs of Edom, in reference to their dwellings, in the land of their possession; he is Esau father of Edom.

37.1: And Jacob dwells in the land of his father's sojournings--in the land of Canaan.
37.2: These are births of Jacob: Joseph, a son of seventeen years, has been enjoying himself with his brethren among the flock, (and he is a youth,) with the sons of Bilhah, and with the sons of Zilpah, his father's wives, and Joseph brings in an account of their evil to their father.
37.3: And Israel has loved Joseph more than any of his sons, for he is a son of his old age, and has made for him a long coat;
37.4: and his brethren see that their father has loved him more than any of his brethren, and they hate him, and have not been able to speak to him peaceably.
37.5: And Joseph dreams a dream, and declares to his brethren, and they add still more to hate him.
37.6: And he says to them, `Hear you, I pray you, this dream which I have dreamed:
37.7: that, indeed, we are binding bundles in the midst of the field, and indeed, my bundle has arisen, and has also stood up, and indeed, your bundles are round about, and bow themselves to my bundle.'
37.8: And his brethren say to him, `Do you certainly reign over us? do you certainly rule over us?' and they add still more to hate him, for his dreams, and for his words.
37.9: And he dreams yet another dream, and recounts it to his brethren, and says, `Indeed, I have dreamed a dream again, and indeed, the sun and the moon, and eleven stars, are bowing themselves to me.'
37.10: And he recounts to his father, and to his brethren; and his father pushes against him, and says to him, `What is this dream which you have dreamt? do we certainly come--I, and your mother, and your brethren--to bow ourselves to you, to the earth?'
37.11: and his brethren are zealous against him, and his father has watched the matter.
37.12: And his brethren go to feed the flock of their father in Shechem,
37.13: and Israel says to Joseph, `Are not your brethren feeding in Shechem? come, and I send you to them;' and he says to him, `Here am I;'
37.14: and he says to him, `Go, I pray you, see the peace of your brethren, and the peace of the flock, and bring me back word;' and he sends him from the valley of Hebron, and he comes to Shechem.
37.15: And a man finds him, and indeed, he is wandering in the field, and the man asks him, saying, `What do you seek?'
37.16: and he says, `My brethren I am seeking, declare to me, I pray you, where they are feeding?'
37.17: And the man says, `They have journeyed from this, for I have heard some saying, Let us go to Dothan,' and Joseph goes after his brethren, and finds them in Dothan.
37.18: And they see him from afar, even before he draws near to them, and they conspire against him to put him to death.
37.19: And they say one to another, `Indeed, this man of the dreams comes;
37.20: and now, come, and we slay him, and cast him into one of the pits, and have said, An evil beast has devoured him; and we see what his dreams are.'
37.21: And Reuben hears, and delivers him out of their hand, and says, `Let us not smite the life;'
37.22: and Reuben says to them, `Shed no blood; cast him into this pit which is in the wilderness, and put not forth a hand upon him,' --in order to deliver him out of their hand, to bring him back to his father.
37.23: And it comes to pass, when Joseph has come to his brethren, that they strip Joseph of his coat, the long coat which is upon him,
37.24: and take him and cast him into the pit, and the pit is empty, there is no water in it.
37.25: And they sit down to eat bread, and they lift up their eyes, and look, and indeed, a company of Ishmaelites coming from Gilead, and their camels bearing spices, and balm, and myrrh, going to take them down to Egypt.
37.26: And Judah says to his brethren, `What gain when we slay our brother, and have concealed his blood?
37.27: Come, and we sell him to the Ishmaelites, and our hands are not on him, for he is our brother--our flesh;' and his brethren hearken.
37.28: And Midianite merchantmen pass by and they draw out and bring up Joseph out of the pit, and sell Joseph to the Ishmaelites for twenty silverlings, and they bring Joseph into Egypt.
37.29: And Reuben returns to the pit, and indeed, Joseph is not in the pit, and he rends his garments,
37.30: and he returns to his brethren, and says, `The lad is not, and I--where am I going?'
37.31: And they take the coat of Joseph, and slaughter a kid of the goats, and dip the coat in the blood,
37.32: and send the long coat, and they bring it in to their father, and say, `This have we found; discern, we pray you, whether it is your son's coat or not?'
37.33: And he discerns it, and says, `My son's coat! an evil beast has devoured him; torn--torn is Joseph!'
37.34: And Jacob rends his raiment, and puts sackcloth on his loins, and becomes a mourner for his son many days,
37.35: and all his sons and all his daughters rise to comfort him, and he refuses to comfort himself, and says, `For--I go down mourning to my son, to Sheol,' and his father weeps for him.
37.36: And the Medanites have sold him to Egypt, to Potiphar, a eunuch of Pharaoh, head of the executioners.

38.1: And it comes to pass, at that time, that Judah goes down from his brethren, and turns aside to a man, an Adullamite, whose name is Hirah;
38.2: and Judah sees there the daughter of a man, a Canaanite, whose name is Shuah, and takes her, and goes in to her.
38.3: And she conceives, and bears a son, and he calls his name Er;
38.4: and she conceives again, and bears a son, and calls his name Onan;
38.5: and she adds again, and bears a son, and calls his name Shelah; and he was in Chezib in her bearing him.
38.6: And Judah takes a wife for Er, his first-born, and her name is Tamar;
38.7: and Er, Judah's first-born, is evil in the eyes of Jehovah, and Jehovah does put him to death.
38.8: And Judah says to Onan, `Go in to the wife of your brother, and marry her, and raise up seed to your brother;'
38.9: and Onan knows that the seed is not reckoned his; and it has come to pass, if he has gone in to his brother's wife, that he has destroyed it to the earth, so as not to give seed to his brother;
38.10: and that which he has done is evil in the eyes of Jehovah, and He puts him also to death.
38.11: And Judah says to Tamar his daughter-in-law, `Abide a widow at your father's house, till Shelah my son grows up;' for he said, `Lest he die--even he--like his brethren;' and Tamar goes and dwells at her father's house.
38.12: And the days are multiplied, and the daughter of Shuah, Judah's wife, dies; and Judah is comforted, and goes up to his sheep-shearers, he and Hirah his friend the Adullamite, to Timnath.
38.13: And it is declared to Tamar, saying, `Indeed, your husband's father is going up to Timnath to shear his flock;'
38.14: and she turns aside the garments of her widowhood from off her, and covers herself with a vail, and wraps herself up, and sits in the opening of Enayim, which is by the way to Timnath, for she has seen that Shelah has grown up, and she has not been given to him for a wife.
38.15: And Judah sees her, and reckons her for a harlot, for she has covered her face,
38.16: and he turns aside to her by the way, and says, `Come, I pray you, let me come in to you,' (for he has not known that she is his daughter-in-law); and she says, `What do you give to me, that you may come in to me?'
38.17: and he says, `I--I send a kid of the goats from the flock.' And she says, `Do you give a pledge till you send it?'
38.18: and he says, `What is the pledge that I give to you?' and she says, `Your seal, and your ribbon, and your staff which is in your hand;' and he gives to her, and goes in to her, and she conceives to him;
38.19: and she rises, and goes, and turns aside her vail from off her, and puts on the garments of her widowhood.
38.20: And Judah sends the kid of the goats by the hand of his friend the Adullamite, to receive the pledge from the hand of the woman, and he has not found her.
38.21: And he asks the men of her place, saying, `Where is the separated one--she in Enayim, by the way?' and they say, `There has not been in this place a separated one.'
38.22: And he turns back to Judah, and says, `I have not found her; and the men of the place also have said, There has not been in this place a separated one,'
38.23: and Judah says, `Let her take to herself, lest we become despised; indeed, I sent this kid, and you have not found her.'
38.24: And it comes to pass about three months after, that it is declared to Judah, saying, `Tamar your daughter-in-law has committed fornication; and also, indeed, she has conceived by fornication:' and Judah says, `Bring her out--and she is burnt.'
38.25: She is brought out, and she has sent to her husband's father, saying, `To a man whose these are, I am pregnant;' and she says, `Discern, I pray you, whose are these--the seal, and the ribbons, and the staff.'
38.26: And Judah discerns and says, `She has been more righteous than I, because that I did not give her to Shelah my son;' and he has not added to know her again.
38.27: And it comes to pass in the time of her bearing, that indeed, twins are in her womb;
38.28: and it comes to pass in her bearing, that one gives out a hand, and the midwife takes and binds on his hand a scarlet thread, saying, `This has come out first.'
38.29: And it comes to pass as he draws back his hand, that indeed, his brother has come out, and she says, `What! you have broken forth--on you is the breach;' and he calls his name Pharez;
38.30: and afterwards has his brother come out, on whose hand is the scarlet thread, and he calls his name Zarah.

39.1: And Joseph has been brought down to Egypt, and Potiphar, a eunuch of Pharaoh, head of the executioners, an Egyptian man, buys him out of the hands of the Ishmaelites who have brought him there.
39.2: And Jehovah is with Joseph, and he is a prosperous man, and he is in the house of his lord the Egyptian,
39.3: and his lord sees that Jehovah is with him, and all that he is doing Jehovah is causing to prosper in his hand,
39.4: and Joseph finds grace in his eyes and serves him, and he appoints him over his house, and all that he has he has given into his hand.
39.5: And it comes to pass from the time that he has appointed him over his house, and over all that he has, that Jehovah blesses the house of the Egyptian for Joseph's sake, and the blessing of Jehovah is on all that he has, in the house, and in the field;
39.6: and he leaves all that he has in the hand of Joseph, and he has not known anything that he has, except the bread which he is eating. And Joseph is of a fair form, and of a fair appearance.
39.7: And it comes to pass after these things, that his lord's wife lifts up her eyes to Joseph, and says, `Lie with me;'
39.8: and he refuses, and says to his lord's wife, `Indeed, my lord has not known what is with me in the house, and all that he has he has given into my hand;
39.9: none is greater in this house than I, and he has not withheld from me anything, except you, because you are his wife; and how shall I do this great evil? --then have I sinned against God.'
39.10: And it comes to pass at her speaking to Joseph day by day, that he has not hearkened to her, to lie near her, to be with her;
39.11: and it comes to pass about this day, that he goes into the house to do his work, and there is none of the men of the house there in the house,
39.12: and she catches him by his garment, saying, `Lie with me;' and he leaves his garment in her hand, and flees, and goes without.
39.13: And it comes to pass when she sees that he has left his garment in her hand, and flees without,
39.14: that she calls for the men of her house, and speaks to them, saying, `See, he has brought in to us a man, a Hebrew, to play with us; he has come in to me, to lie with me, and I call with a loud voice,
39.15: and it comes to pass, when he hears that I have lifted up my voice and call, that he leaves his garment near me, and flees, and goes without.'
39.16: And she places his garment near her, until the coming in of his lord to his house.
39.17: And she speaks to him according to these words, saying, `The Hebrew servant whom you have brought to us, has come in to me to play with me;
39.18: and it comes to pass, when I lift my voice and call, that he leaves his garment near me, and flees without.'
39.19: And it comes to pass when his lord hears the words of his wife, which she has spoken to him, saying, `According to these things has your servant done to me,' that his anger burns;
39.20: and Joseph's lord takes him, and puts him to the round-house, a place where the king's prisoners are bound; and he is there in the round-house.
39.21: And Jehovah is with Joseph, and stretches out kindness to him, and puts his grace in the eyes of the chief of the round-house;
39.22: and the chief of the round-house gives into the hand of Joseph all the prisoners who are in the round-house, and of all that they are doing there, he has been doer;
39.23: the chief of the round-house sees not anything under his hand, because Jehovah is with him, and that which he is doing Jehovah is causing to prosper.

40.1: And it comes to pass, after these things--the butler of the king of Egypt and the baker have sinned against their lord, against the king of Egypt;
40.2: and Pharaoh is wroth against his two eunuchs, against the chief of the butlers, and against the chief of the bakers,
40.3: and gives them in charge in the house of the chief of the executioners, to the round-house, the place where Joseph is a prisoner,
40.4: and the chief of the executioners charges Joseph with them, and he serves them; and they are days in charge.
40.5: And they dream a dream both of them, each his dream in one night, each according to the interpretation of his dream, the butler and the baker whom the king of Egypt has, who are prisoners in the round-house.
40.6: And Joseph comes in to them in the morning, and sees them, and indeed, they are morose;
40.7: and he asks Pharaoh's eunuchs who are with him in charge in the house of his lord, saying, `Wherefore are your faces sad to-day?'
40.8: And they say to him, `A dream we have dreamed, and there is no interpreter of it;' and Joseph says to them, `Are not interpretations with God? recount, I pray you, to me.'
40.9: And the chief of the butlers recounts his dream to Joseph, and says to him, `In my dream, then indeed, a vine is before me!
40.10: and in the vine are three branches, and it is as it were flourishing; gone up has its blossom, its clusters have ripened grapes;
40.11: and Pharaoh's cup is in my hand, and I take the grapes and press them into the cup of Pharaoh, and I give the cup into the hand of Pharaoh.'
40.12: And Joseph says to him, `This is its interpretation: the three branches are three days;
40.13: yet, within three days does Pharaoh lift up your head, and has put you back on your station, and you have given the cup of Pharaoh into his hand, according to the former custom when you were his butler.
40.14: `Surely if you have remembered me with you, when it is well with you, and have done (I pray you) kindness with me, and have made mention of me to Pharaoh, then have you brought me out from this house,
40.15: for I was really stolen from the land of the Hebrews; and here also have I done nothing that they have put me in the pit.'
