40.16: And the chief of the bakers sees that he has interpreted good, and he says to Joseph, `I also am in a dream, and indeed, three baskets of white bread are on my head,
40.17: and in the uppermost basket are of all kinds of Pharaoh's food, work of a baker; and the birds are eating them out of the basket, from off my head.'
40.18: And Joseph answers and says, `This is its interpretation: the three baskets are three days;
40.19: yet, within three days does Pharaoh lift up your head from off you, and has hanged you on a tree, and the birds have eaten your flesh from off you.'
40.20: And it comes to pass, on the third day, Pharaoh's birthday, that he makes a banquet to all his servants, and lifts up the head of the chief of the butlers, and the head of the chief of the bakers among his servants,
40.21: and he puts back the chief of the butlers to his butlership, and he gives the cup into the hand of Pharaoh;
40.22: and the chief of the bakers he has hanged, as Joseph has interpreted to them;
40.23: and the chief of the butlers has not remembered Joseph, but forgets him.

41.1: And it comes to pass, at the end of two years of days that Pharaoh is dreaming, and indeed, he is standing by the River,
41.2: and indeed, from the River coming up are seven kine, of fair appearance, and fat in flesh, and they feed among the reeds;
41.3: and indeed, seven other kine are coming up after them out of the River, of bad appearance, and lean in flesh, and they stand near the kine on the edge of the River,
41.4: and the kine of bad appearance and lean in flesh eat up the seven kine of fair appearance, and fat--and Pharaoh awakes.
41.5: And he sleeps, and dreams a second time, and indeed, seven ears are coming up on one stalk, fat and good,
41.6: and indeed, seven ears, thin, and blasted with an east wind, are springing up after them;
41.7: and the thin ears swallow the seven fat and full ears--and Pharaoh awakes, and indeed, a dream.
41.8: And it comes to pass in the morning, that his spirit is moved, and he sends and calls all the scribes of Egypt, and all its wise men, and Pharaoh recounts to them his dream, and there is no interpreter of them to Pharaoh.
41.9: And the chief of the butlers speaks with Pharaoh, saying, `My sin I mention this day:
41.10: Pharaoh has been wroth against his servants, and gives me into charge in the house of the chief of the executioners, me and the chief of the bakers;
41.11: and we dream a dream in one night, I and he, each according to the interpretation of his dream we have dreamed.
41.12: And there is with us a youth, a Hebrew, servant to the chief of the executioners, and we recount to him, and he interprets to us our dreams, to each according to his dream has he interpreted,
41.13: and it comes to pass, as he has interpreted to us so it has been, me he put back on my station, and him he hanged.'
41.14: And Pharaoh sends and calls Joseph, and they cause him to run out of the pit, and he shaves, and changes his garments, and comes in to Pharaoh.
41.15: And Pharaoh says to Joseph, `A dream I have dreamed, and there is no interpreter of it, and I--I have heard concerning you, saying, You understand a dream to interpret it,'
41.16: and Joseph answers Pharaoh, saying, `Without me--God does answer Pharaoh with peace.'
41.17: And Pharaoh speaks to Joseph: `In my dream, indeed, I am standing by the edge of the River,
41.18: and indeed, out of the River coming up are seven kine, fat in flesh, and of fair form, and they feed among the reeds;
41.19: and indeed, seven other kine are coming up after them, thin, and of very bad form, and lean in flesh; I have not seen like these in all the land of Egypt for badness.
41.20: `And the lean and the bad kine eat up the first seven fat kine,
41.21: and they come in to their midst, and it has not been known that they have come in to their midst, and their appearance is bad as at the commencement; and I awake.
41.22: `And I see in my dream, and indeed, seven ears are coming up on one stalk, full and good;
41.23: and indeed, seven ears, withered, thin, blasted with an east wind, are springing up after them;
41.24: and the thin ears swallow the seven good ears; and I tell to the scribes, and there is none declaring to me.'
41.25: And Joseph says to Pharaoh, `The dream of Pharaoh is one: that which God is doing he has declared to Pharaoh;
41.26: the seven good kine are seven years, and the seven good ears are seven years, the dream is one;
41.27: and the seven thin and bad kine which are coming up after them are seven years, and the seven empty ears, blasted with an east wind, are seven years of famine;
41.28: this is the thing which I have spoken to Pharaoh: That which God is doing, he has shown Pharaoh.
41.29: `Indeed, seven years are coming of great abundance in all the land of Egypt,
41.30: and seven years of famine have arisen after them, and all the plenty is forgotten in the land of Egypt, and the famine has finished the land,
41.31: and the plenty is not known in the land because of that famine afterwards, for it is very grievous.
41.32: `And because of the repeating of the dream to Pharaoh twice, surely the thing is established by God, and God is hastening to do it.
41.33: `And now, let Pharaoh provide a man, intelligent and wise, and set him over the land of Egypt;
41.34: let Pharaoh make and appoint overseers over the land, and receive a fifth of the land of Egypt in the seven years of plenty,
41.35: and they gather all the food of these good years that are coming, and heap up corn under the hand of Pharaoh--food in the cities; and they have kept it,
41.36: and the food has been for a store for the land, for the seven years of famine which are in the land of Egypt; and the land is cut off by the famine.'
41.37: And the thing is good in the eyes of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of all his servants,
41.38: and Pharaoh says to his servants, `Do we find like this, a man in whom the spirit of God is?'
41.39: and Pharaoh says to Joseph, `After God's causing you to know all this, there is none intelligent and wise as you;
41.40: you--you are over my house, and at your mouth do all my people kiss; only in the throne I am greater than you.'
41.41: And Pharaoh says to Joseph, `See, I have put you over all the land of Egypt.'
41.42: And Pharaoh turns aside his seal-ring from off his hand, and puts it on the hand of Joseph, and clothes him with garments of fine linen, and places a chain of gold on his neck,
41.43: and causes him to ride in the second chariot which he has, and they proclaim before him, `Bow the knee!' and--to put him over all the land of Egypt.
41.44: And Pharaoh says to Joseph, `I am Pharaoh, and without you a man does not lift up his hand and his foot in all the land of Egypt;'
41.45: and Pharaoh calls Joseph's name Zaphnath-Paaneah, and he gives to him Asenath daughter of Poti-Pherah, priest of On, for a wife, and Joseph goes out over the land of Egypt.
41.46: And Joseph is a son of thirty years in his standing before Pharaoh king of Egypt, and Joseph goes out from the presence of Pharaoh, and passes over through all the land of Egypt;
41.47: and the land makes in the seven years of plenty by handfuls.
41.48: And he gathers all the food of the seven years which have been in the land of Egypt, and puts food in the cities; the food of the field which is round about each city has he put in its midst;
41.49: and Joseph gathers corn as sand of the sea, multiplying exceedingly, until that he has ceased to number, for there is no number.
41.50: And to Joseph were born two sons before the year of famine comes, whom Asenath daughter of Poti-Pherah, priest of On, has borne to him,
41.51: and Joseph calls the name of the first-born Manasseh: `for, God has made me to forget all my labour, and all the house of my father;'
41.52: and the name of the second he has called Ephraim: `for, God has caused me to be fruitful in the land of my affliction.'
41.53: And the seven years of plenty are completed which have been in the land of Egypt,
41.54: and the seven years of famine begin to come, as Joseph said, and famine is in all the lands, but in all the land of Egypt has been bread;
41.55: and all the land of Egypt is famished, and the people cries to Pharaoh for bread, and Pharaoh says to all the Egyptians, `Go to Joseph; that which he says to you--do.'
41.56: And the famine has been over all the face of the land, and Joseph opens all places which have corn in them, and sells to the Egyptians; and the famine is severe in the land of Egypt,
41.57: and all the earth has come to Egypt, to buy, to Joseph, for the famine was severe in all the earth.

42.1: And Jacob sees that there is corn in Egypt, and Jacob says to his sons, `Why do you look at each other?'
42.2: he says also, `Indeed, I have heard that there is corn in Egypt, go down there, and buy for us from from there, and we live and do not die;'
42.3: and the ten brethren of Joseph go down to buy corn in Egypt,
42.4: and Benjamin, Joseph's brother, Jacob has not sent with his brethren, for he said, `Lest mischief meet him.'
42.5: And the sons of Israel come to buy in the midst of those coming, for the famine has been in the land of Canaan,
42.6: and Joseph is the ruler over the land, he who is selling to all the people of the land, and Joseph's brethren come and bow themselves to him--face to the earth.
42.7: And Joseph sees his brethren, and discerns them, and makes himself strange to them, and speaks with them sharp things, and says to them, `From from where have you come?' and they say, `From the land of Canaan--to buy food.'
42.8: And Joseph discerns his brethren, but they have not discerned him,
42.9: and Joseph remembers the dreams which he dreamed of them, and says to them, `You are spies; to see the nakedness of the land you have come.'
42.10: And they say to him, `No, my lord, but your servants have come to buy food;
42.11: we are all of us sons of one man, we are right men; your servants have not been spies;'
42.12: and he says to them, `No, but the nakedness of the land you have come to see;'
42.13: and they say, `Your servants are twelve brethren; we are sons of one man in the land of Canaan, and indeed, the young one is with our father to-day, and the one is not.'
42.14: And Joseph says to them, `This is that which I have spoken to you, saying, You are spies,
42.15: by this you are proved: Pharaoh lives! if you go out from this--except by your young brother coming here;
42.16: send one of you, and let him bring your brother, and you, remain you bound, and let your words be proved, whether truth be with you: and if not--Pharaoh lives! surely you are spies;'
42.17: and he removes them to charge three days.
42.18: And Joseph says to them on the third day, `This do and live; God I fear!
42.19: if you are right men, let one of your brethren be bound in the house of your ward, and you, go, carry in corn for the famine of your houses,
42.20: and your young brother you bring to me, and your words are established, and you die not;' and they do so.
42.21: And they say one to another, `Truly we are guilty concerning our brother, because we saw the distress of his soul, in his making supplication to us, and we did not hearken: therefore has this distress come upon us.'
42.22: And Reuben answers them, saying, `Spoke I not to you, saying, Sin not against the lad? and you hearkened not; and his blood also, indeed, it is required.'
42.23: And they have not known that Joseph understands, for the interpreter is between them;
42.24: and he turns round from them, and weeps, and turns back to them, and speaks to them, and takes from them Simeon, and binds him before their eyes.
42.25: And Joseph commands, and they fill their vessels with corn, also to put back the money of each to his sack, and to give to them provision for the way; and one does to them so.
42.26: And they lift up their corn upon their asses, and go from from there,
42.27: and the one opens his sack to give provender to his ass at a lodging-place, and he sees his money, and indeed, it is in the mouth of his bag,
42.28: and he says to his brethren, `My money has been put back, and also, indeed, in my bag:' and their heart goes out, and they tremble, one to another saying, `What is this God has done to us!'
42.29: And they come in to Jacob their father, to the land of Canaan, and they declare to him all the things meeting them, saying,
42.30: `The man, the lord of the land, has spoken with us sharp things, and makes us as spies of the land;
42.31: and we say to him, We are right men, we have not been spies,
42.32: we are twelve brethren, sons of our father, the one is not, and the young one is to-day with our father in the land of Canaan.
42.33: `And the man, the lord of the land, says to us, By this I know that you are right men--one of your brethren leave with me, and for the famine of your houses take you and go,
42.34: and bring your young brother to me, and I know that you are not spies, but you are right men; your brother I give to you, and you trade with the land.'
42.35: And it comes to pass, they are emptying their sacks, and indeed, the bundle of each man's silver is in his sack, and they see their bundles of silver, they and their father, and are afraid;
42.36: and Jacob their father says to them, `Me you have bereaved; Joseph is not, and Simeon is not, and Benjamin you take--against me have been all these.'
42.37: And Reuben speaks to his father, saying, `My two sons you do put to death, if I bring him not in to you; give him into my hand, and I--I bring him back to you;'
42.38: and he says, `My son does not go down with you, for his brother is dead, and he by himself is left; when mischief has met him in the way in which you go, then you have brought down my grey hairs in sorrow to sheol.'

43.1: And the famine is severe in the land;
43.2: and it comes to pass, when they have finished eating the corn which they brought from Egypt, that their father says to them, `Turn back, buy for us a little food.'
43.3: And Judah speaks to him, saying, `The man protesting protested to us, saying, You do not see my face without your brother being with you;
43.4: if you are sending our brother with us, we go down, and buy for you food,
43.5: and if you are not sending--we do not go down, for the man said to us, You do not see my face without your brother being with you.'
43.6: And Israel says, `Why did you evil to me, by declaring to the man that you had yet a brother?'
43.7: and they say, `The man asked diligently concerning us, and concerning our kindred, saying, Is your father yet alive? have you a brother? and we declare to him according to the tenor of these things; do we certainly know that he will say, Bring down your brother?'
43.8: And Judah says to Israel his father, `Send the youth with me, and we arise, and go, and live, and do not die, both we, and you, and our infants.
43.9: I--I am surety for him, from my hand you do require him; if I have not brought him in to you, and set him before you--then I have sinned against you all the days;
43.10: for if we had not lingered, surely now we had returned these two times.'
43.11: And Israel their father says to them, `If so, now, this do: take of the praised thing of the land in your vessels, and take down to the man a present, a little balm, and a little honey, spices and myrrh, nuts and almonds;
43.12: and double money take in your hand, even the money which is brought back in the mouth of your bags, you take back in your hand, it may be it is an oversight.
43.13: `And take your brother, and rise, turn back to the man;
43.14: and God Almighty give to you mercies before the man, so that he has sent to you your other brother and Benjamin; and I, when I am bereaved--I am bereaved.'
43.15: And the men take this present, double money also they have taken in their hand, and Benjamin; and they rise, and go down to Egypt, and stand before Joseph;
43.16: and Joseph sees Benjamin with them, and says to him who is over his house, `Bring the men into the house, and slaughter an animal, and make ready, for with me do the men eat at noon.'
43.17: And the man does as Joseph has said, and the man brings in the men into the house of Joseph,
43.18: and the men are afraid because they have been brought into the house of Joseph, and they say, `For the matter of the money which was put back in our bags at the commencement are we brought in--to roll himself upon us, and to throw himself on us, and to take us for servants--our asses also.'
43.19: And they come nigh to the man who is over the house of Joseph, and speak to him at the opening of the house,
43.20: and say, `O, my lord, we really come down at the commencement to buy food;
43.21: and it comes to pass, when we have come in to the lodging-place, and open our bags, that indeed, each one's money is in the mouth of his bag, our money in its weight, and we bring it back in our hand;
43.22: and other money have we brought down in our hand to buy food; we have not known who put our money in our bags.'
43.23: And he says, `Peace to you, fear not: your God and the God of your father has given to you hidden treasure in your bags, your money came to me;' and he brings out Simeon to them.
43.24: And the man brings in the men into Joseph's house, and gives water, and they wash their feet; and he gives provender for their asses,
43.25: and they prepare the present until the coming of Joseph at noon, for they have heard that there they do eat bread.
43.26: And Joseph comes into the house, and they bring to him the present which is in their hand, into the house, and bow themselves to him, to the earth;
43.27: and he asks of them of peace, and says, `Is your father well? the aged man of whom you have spoken, is he yet alive?'
43.28: and they say, `Your servant our father is well, he is yet alive;' and they bow, and do obeisance.
43.29: And he lifts up his eyes, and sees Benjamin his brother, his mother's son, and says, `Is this your young brother, of whom you have spoken to me?' and he says, `God favour you, my son.'
43.30: And Joseph hastes, for his bowels have been moved for his brother, and he seeks to weep, and enters the inner chamber, and weeps there;
43.31: and he washes his face, and goes out, and refrains himself, and says, `Place bread.'
43.32: And they place for him by himself, and for them by themselves, and for the Egyptians who are eating with him by themselves: for the Egyptians are unable to eat bread with the Hebrews, for it is an abomination to the Egyptians.
43.33: And they sit before him, the first-born according to his birthright, and the young one according to his youth, and the men wonder one at another;
43.34: and he lifts up gifts from before him to them, and the gift of Benjamin is five hands more than the gifts of all of them; and they drink, yes, they drink abundantly with him.

44.1: And he commands him who is over his house, saying, `Fill the bags of the men with food, as they are able to bear, and put the money of each in the mouth of his bag;
44.2: and my cup, the silver cup, you do put in the mouth of the bag of the young one, and his corn-money;' and he does according to the word of Joseph which he has spoken.
44.3: The morning is bright, and the men have been sent away, they and their asses--
44.4: they have gone out of the city--they have not gone far off--and Joseph has said to him who is over his house, `Rise, pursue after the men; and you have overtaken them, and you have said to them, Why have you recompensed evil for good?
44.5: Is not this that with which my lord drinks? and he observes diligently with it; you have done evil in that which you have done.'
44.6: And he overtakes them, and speaks to them these words,
44.7: and they say to him, `Why does my lord speak according to these words? far be it from your servants to do according to this word;
44.8: indeed, the money which we found in the mouth of our bags we brought back to you from the land of Canaan, and how do we steal from the house of your lord silver or gold?
44.9: with whomever of your servants it is found, he has died, and we also are to my lord for servants.'
44.10: And he says, `Now, also, according to your words, so it is; he with whom it is found becomes my servant, and you are acquitted;'
44.11: and they hasten and take down each his bag to the earth, and each opens his bag;
44.12: and he searches--at the eldest he has begun, and at the youngest he has completed--and the cup is found in the bag of Benjamin;
44.13: and they rend their garments, and each lades his ass, and they turn back to the city.
44.14: And Judah--his brethren also--comes in to the house of Joseph, and he is yet there, and they fall before him to the earth;
44.15: and Joseph says to them, `What is this deed that you have done? have you not known that a man like me does diligently observe?'
44.16: And Judah says, `What do we say to my lord? what do we speak? and what--do we justify ourselves? God has found out the iniquity of your servants; indeed, we are servants to my lord, both we, and he in whose hand the cup has been found;'
44.17: and he says, `Far be it from me to do this; the man in whose hand the cup has been found, he becomes my servant; and you, go you up in peace to your father.'
44.18: And Judah comes nigh to him, and says, `O, my lord, let your servant speak, I pray you, a word in the ears of my lord, and let not your anger burn against your servant--for you are as Pharaoh.
44.19: My lord has asked his servants, saying, Have you a father or brother?
44.20: and we say to my lord, We have a father, an aged one, and a child of old age, a little one; and his brother died, and he is left alone of his mother, and his father has loved him.
44.21: `And you say to your servants, Bring him down to me, and I set my eye upon him;
44.22: and we say to my lord, The youth is not able to leave his father, when he has left his father, then he has died;
44.23: and you say to your servants, If your young brother come not down with you, you add not to see my face.
44.24: `And it comes to pass, that we have come up to your servant my father, that we declare to him the words of my lord;
44.25: and our father says, Turn back, buy for us a little food,
44.26: and we say, We are not able to go down; if our young brother is with us, then we have gone down; for we are not able to see the man's face, and our young brother not with us.
44.27: `And your servant my father says to us, You--you have known that two did my wife bare to me,
44.28: and the one goes out from me, and I say, Surely he is torn--torn! and I have not seen him since;
44.29: when you have taken also this from my presence, and mischief has met him, then you have brought down my grey hairs with evil to sheol.
44.30: `And now, at my coming in to your servant my father, and the youth not with us (and his soul is bound up in his soul),
44.31: then it has come to pass when he sees that the youth is not, that he has died, and your servants have brought down the grey hairs of your servant our father with sorrow to sheol;
44.32: for your servant obtained the youth by surety from my father, saying, If I bring him not in to you--then I have sinned against my father all the days.
44.33: `And now, let your servant, I pray you, abide instead of the youth a servant to my lord, and the youth goes up with his brethren,
44.34: for how do I go up to my father, and the youth not with me? lest I look on the evil which does find my father.'

45.1: And Joseph has not been able to refrain himself before all those standing by him, and he calls, `Put out every man from me;' and no man has stood with him when Joseph makes himself known to his brethren,
45.2: and he gives forth his voice in weeping, and the Egyptians hear, and the house of Pharaoh hears.
45.3: And Joseph says to his brethren, `I am Joseph, is my father yet alive?' and his brethren have not been able to answer him, for they have been troubled at his presence.
45.4: And Joseph says to his brethren, `Come nigh to me, I pray you,' and they come nigh; and he says, `I am Joseph, your brother, whom you sold into Egypt;
45.5: and now, be not grieved, nor let it be displeasing in your eyes that you sold me here, for to preserve life has God sent me before you.
45.6: `Because these two years the famine is in the heart of the land, and yet are five years, in which there is neither ploughing nor harvest;
45.7: and God sends me before you, to place of you a remnant in the land, and to give life to you by a great escape;
45.8: and now, you--you have not sent me here, but God, and He does set me for a father to Pharaoh, and for lord to all his house, and ruler over all the land of Egypt.
45.9: `Haste, and go up to my father, then you have said to him, Thus said Joseph your son, God has set me for lord to all Egypt; come down to me, stay not,
45.10: and you have dwelt in the land of Goshen, and been near to me, you and your sons, and your son's sons, and your flock, and your herd, and all that you have,
45.11: and I have nourished you there--for yet are five years of famine--lest you become poor, you and your household, and all that you have.
45.12: `And indeed, your eyes are seeing, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin, that it is my mouth which is speaking to you;
45.13: and you have declared to my father all my honour in Egypt, and all that you have seen, and you have hasted, and have brought down my father here.'
45.14: And he falls on the neck of Benjamin his brother, and weeps, and Benjamin has wept on his neck;
45.15: and he kisses all his brethren, and weeps over them; and afterwards have his brethren spoken with him.
45.16: And the sound has been heard in the house of Pharaoh, saying, `Come have the brethren of Joseph;' and it is good in the eyes of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of his servants,
45.17: and Pharaoh says to Joseph, `Say to your brethren, This do you: lade your beasts, and go, enter you the land of Canaan,
45.18: and take your father, and your households, and come to me, and I give to you the good of the land of Egypt, and eat you the fat of the land.
45.19: `Yes, you--you have been commanded: this do you, take for yourselves out of the land of Egypt, waggons for your infants, and for your wives, and you have brought your father, and come;
45.20: and your eye has no pity on your vessels, for the good of all the land of Egypt is yours.'
45.21: And the sons of Israel do so, and Joseph gives waggons to them by the command of Pharaoh, and he gives to them provision for the way;
45.22: to all of them has he given--to each changes of garments, and to Benjamin he has given three hundred silverlings, and five changes of garments;
45.23: and to his father he has sent thus: ten asses bearing of the good things of Egypt, and ten she-asses bearing corn and bread, even food for his father for the way.
45.24: And he sends his brethren away, and they go; and he says to them, `Be not angry in the way.'
45.25: And they go up out of Egypt, and come in to the land of Canaan, to Jacob their father,
45.26: and they declare to him, saying, `Joseph is yet alive,' and that he is ruler over all the land of Egypt; and his heart ceases, for he has not given credence to them.
45.27: And they speak to him all the words of Joseph, which he has spoken to them, and he sees the waggons which Joseph has sent to bear him away, and live does the spirit of Jacob their father;
45.28: and Israel says, `Enough! Joseph my son is yet alive; I go and see him before I die.'

46.1: And Israel journeys, and all that he has, and comes in to Beer-Sheba, and sacrifices sacrifices to the God of his father Isaac;
46.2: and God speaks to Israel in visions of the night, and says, `Jacob, Jacob;' and he says, `Here am I.'
46.3: And He says, `I am God, God of your father, be not afraid of going down to Egypt, for for a great nation I set you there;
46.4: I--I go down with you to Egypt, and I--I also certainly bring you up, and Joseph does put his hand on your eyes.'
46.5: And Jacob rises from Beer-Sheba, and the sons of Israel bear away Jacob their father, And their infants, and their wives, in the waggons which Pharaoh has sent to bear him,
46.6: and they take their cattle, and their goods which they have acquired in the land of Canaan, and come into Egypt--Jacob, and all his seed with him,
46.7: his sons, and his sons' sons with him, his daughters, and his sons' daughters, yes, all his seed he brought with him into Egypt.
46.8: And these are the names of the sons of Israel who are coming into Egypt: Jacob and his sons, Jacob's first-born, Reuben.
46.9: And sons of Reuben: Hanoch, and Phallu, and Hezron, and Carmi.
46.10: And sons of Simeon: Jemuel, and Jamin, and Ohad, and Jachin, and Zohar, and Shaul son of the Canaanitess.
46.11: And sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
46.12: And sons of Judah: Er, and Onan, and Shelah, and Pharez, and Zarah, (and Er and Onan die in the land of Canaan.) And sons of Pharez are Hezron and Hamul.
46.13: And sons of Issachar: Tola, and Phuvah, and Job, and Shimron.
46.14: And sons of Zebulun: Sered, and Elon, and Jahleel.
46.15: These are sons of Leah whom she bare to Jacob in Padan-Aram, and Dinah his daughter; all the persons of his sons and his daughters are thirty and three.
46.16: And sons of Gad: Ziphion, and Haggi, Shuni, and Ezbon, Eri, and Arodi, and Areli.
46.17: And sons of Asher: Jimnah, and Ishuah, and Isui, and Beriah, and Serah their sister. And sons of Beriah: Heber and Malchiel.
46.18: These are sons of Zilpah, whom Laban gave to Leah his daughter, and she bears these to Jacob--sixteen persons.
46.19: Sons of Rachel, Jacob's wife: Joseph and Benjamin.
46.20: And born to Joseph in the land of Egypt (whom Asenath daughter of Poti-Pherah, priest of On, has borne to him) are Manasseh and Ephraim.
46.21: And sons of Benjamin: Belah, and Becher, and Ashbel, Gera, and Naaman, Ehi, and Rosh, Muppim, and Huppim, and Ard.
46.22: These are sons of Rachel, who were born to Jacob; all the persons are fourteen.
46.24: And sons of Naphtali: Jahzeel, and Guni, and Jezer, and Shillem.
46.25: These are sons of Bilhah, whom Laban gave to Rachel his daughter; and she bears these to Jacob--all the persons are seven.
46.26: All the persons who are coming to Jacob to Egypt, coming out of his thigh, apart from the wives of Jacob's sons, all the persons are sixty and six.
46.27: And the sons of Joseph who have been born to him in Egypt are two persons. All the persons of the house of Jacob who are coming into Egypt are seventy.
46.28: And Judah he has sent before him to Joseph, to direct before him to Goshen, and they come into the land of Goshen;
46.29: and Joseph harnesses his chariot, and goes up to meet Israel his father, to Goshen, and appears to him, and falls on his neck, and weeps on his neck again;
46.30: and Israel says to Joseph, `Let me die this time, after my seeing your face, for you are yet alive.'
46.31: And Joseph says to his brethren, and to the house of his father, `I go up, and declare to Pharaoh, and say to him, My brethren, and the house of my father who are in the land of Canaan have come in to me;
46.32: and the men are feeders of a flock, for they have been men of cattle; and their flock, and their herd, and all that they have, they have brought.'
46.33: `And it has come to pass when Pharaoh calls for you, and has said, What are your works?
46.34: that you have said, Your servants have been men of cattle from our youth, even until now, both we and our fathers, --in order that you may dwell in the land of Goshen, for the abomination of the Egyptians is every one feeding a flock.'

47.1: And Joseph comes, and declares to Pharaoh, and says, `My father, and my brethren, and their flock, and their herd, and all they have, have come from the land of Canaan, and indeed, they are in the land of Goshen.'
47.2: And out of his brethren he has taken five men, and sets them before Pharaoh;
47.3: and Pharaoh says to his brethren, `What are your works?' and they say to Pharaoh, `Your servants are feeders of a flock, both we and our fathers;'
47.4: and they say to Pharaoh, `To sojourn in the land we have come, for there is no pasture for the flock which your servants have, for grievous is the famine in the land of Canaan; and now, let your servants, we pray you, dwell in the land of Goshen.'
47.5: And Pharaoh speaks to Joseph, saying, `Your father and your brethren have come to you:
47.6: the land of Egypt is before you; in the best of the land cause your father and your brethren to dwell--they dwell in the land of Goshen, and if you have known, and there are among them men of ability, then you have set them heads over the cattle I have.'
47.7: And Joseph brings in Jacob his father, and causes him to stand before Pharaoh; and Jacob blesses Pharaoh.
47.8: And Pharaoh says to Jacob, `How many are the days of the years of your life?'
47.9: And Jacob says to Pharaoh, `The days of the years of my sojournings are an hundred and thirty years; few and evil have been the days of the years of my life, and they have not reached the days of the years of the life of my fathers, in the days of their sojournings.'
47.10: And Jacob blesses Pharaoh, and goes out from before Pharaoh.
47.11: And Joseph settles his father and his brethren, and gives to them a possession in the land of Egypt, in the best of the land, in the land of Rameses, as Pharaoh commanded;
47.12: and Joseph nourishes his father, and his brethren, and all the house of his father with bread, according to the mouth of the infants.
47.13: And there is no bread in all the land, for the famine is very grievous, and the land of Egypt and the land of Canaan are feeble because of the famine;
47.14: and Joseph gathers all the silver that is found in the land of Egypt, and in the land of Canaan, for the corn that they are buying, and Joseph brings the silver into the house of Pharaoh.
47.15: And the silver is consumed out of the land of Egypt, and out of the land of Canaan, and all the Egyptians come in to Joseph, saying, `Give to us bread--why do we die before you, though the money has ceased?'
47.16: and Joseph says, `Give your cattle; and I give to you for your cattle, if the money has ceased.'
47.17: And they bring in their cattle to Joseph, and Joseph gives to them bread, for the horses, and for the cattle of the flock, and for the cattle of the herd, and for the asses; and he tends them with bread, for all their cattle, during that year.
47.18: And that year is finished, and they come in to him on the second year, and say to him, `We do not hide from my lord, that since the money has been finished, and possession of the cattle is to my lord, there has not been left before my lord save our bodies, and our ground;
47.19: why do we die before your eyes, both we and our ground? buy us and our ground for bread, and we and our ground are servants to Pharaoh; and give seed, and we live, and die not, and the ground is not desolate.'
47.20: And Joseph buys all the ground of Egypt for Pharaoh, for the Egyptians have sold each his field, for the famine has been severe upon them, and the land becomes Pharaoh's;
47.21: as to the people he has removed them to cities from the one end of the border of Egypt even to its other end.
47.22: Only the ground of the priests he has not bought, for the priests have a portion from Pharaoh, and they have eaten their portion which Pharaoh has given to them, therefore they have not sold their ground.
47.23: And Joseph says to the people, `Indeed, I have bought you to-day and your ground for Pharaoh; indeed, seed for you, and you have sown the ground,
47.24: and it has come to pass in the increases, that you have given a fifth to Pharaoh, and four of the parts are for yourselves, for seed of the field, and for your food, and for those who are in your houses, and for food for your infants.'
47.25: And they say, `You have revived us; we find grace in the eyes of my lord, and have been servants to Pharaoh;'
47.26: and Joseph sets it for a statute to this day, concerning the ground of Egypt, that Pharaoh has a fifth; only the ground of the priests alone has not become Pharaoh's.
47.27: And Israel dwells in the land of Egypt, in the land of Goshen, and they have possession in it, and are fruitful, and multiply exceedingly;
47.28: and Jacob lives in the land of Egypt seventeen years, and the days of Jacob, the years of his life, are an hundred and forty and seven years.
47.29: And the days of Israel are near to die, and he calls for his son, for Joseph, and says to him, `If, I pray you, I have found grace in your eyes, put, I pray you, your hand under my thigh, and you have done with me kindness and truth; bury me not, I pray you, in Egypt,
47.30: and I have lain with my fathers, and you have borne me out of Egypt, and buried me in their burying-place.' And he says, `I--I do according to your word;'
47.31: and he says, `Swear to me;' and he swears to him, and Israel bows himself on the head of the bed.

48.1: And it comes to pass, after these things, that one says to Joseph, `Indeed, your father is sick;' and he takes his two sons with him, Manasseh and Ephraim.
48.2: And one declares to Jacob, and says, `Indeed, your son Joseph is coming to you;' and Israel does strengthen himself, and sit upon the bed.
48.3: And Jacob says to Joseph, `God Almighty has appeared to me, in Luz, in the land of Canaan, and blesses me,
48.4: and says to me, Indeed, I am making you fruitful, and have multiplied you, and given you for an assembly of peoples, and given this land to your seed after you, a possession age-during.
48.5: `And now, your two sons, who are born to you in the land of Egypt, before my coming to you to Egypt, my they are; Ephraim and Manasseh, as Reuben and Simeon they are mine;
48.6: and your family which you have begotten after them are yours; by the name of their brethren they are called in their inheritance.
48.7: `And I--in my coming in from Padan- Aram Rachel has died by me in the land of Canaan, in the way, while yet a kibrath of land to enter Ephrata, and I bury her there in the way of Ephrata, which is Bethlehem.'
48.8: And Israel sees the sons of Joseph, and says, `Who are these?'
48.9: and Joseph says to his father, `They are my sons, whom God has given to me in this place;' and he says, `Bring them, I pray you, to me, and I bless them.'
48.10: And the eyes of Israel have been heavy from age, he is unable to see; and he brings them nigh to him, and he kisses them, and cleaves to them;
48.11: and Israel says to Joseph, `To see your face I had not thought, and indeed, God has showed me also your seed.'
48.12: And Joseph brings them out from between his knees, and bows himself on his face to the earth;
48.13: and Joseph takes them both, Ephraim in his right hand toward Israel's left, and Manasseh in his left toward Israel's right, and brings them nigh to him.
48.14: And Israel puts out his right hand, and places it upon the head of Ephraim, who is the younger, and his left hand upon the head of Manasseh; he has guided his hands wisely, for Manasseh is the first-born.
48.15: And he blesses Joseph, and says, `God, before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac walked habitually: God who is feeding me from my being to this day:
48.16: the Messenger who is redeeming me from all evil does bless the youths, and my name is called upon them, and the name of my fathers Abraham and Isaac; and they increase into a multitude in the midst of the land.'
48.17: And Joseph sees that his father sets his right hand on the head of Ephraim, and it is wrong in his eyes, and he supports the hand of his father to turn it aside from off the head of Ephraim to the head of Manasseh;
48.18: and Joseph says to his father, `Not so, my father, for this is the first-born; set your right hand on his head.'
48.19: And his father refuses, and says, `I have known, my son, I have known; he also becomes a people, and he also is great, and yet, his young brother is greater than he, and his seed is the fulness of the nations;'
48.20: and he blesses them in that day, saying, `By you does Israel bless, saying, God set you as Ephraim and as Manasseh;' and he sets Ephraim before Manasseh.
48.21: And Israel says to Joseph, `Indeed, I am dying, and God has been with you, and has brought you back to the land of your fathers;
48.22: and I--I have given to you one portion above your brethren, which I have taken out of the hand of the Amorite by my sword and by my bow.'

49.1: And Jacob calls to his sons and says, `Be gathered together, and I declare to you that which does happen with you in the latter end of the days.
49.2: `Be assembled, and hear, sons of Jacob, And hearken to Israel your father.
49.3: Reuben! my first-born you, My power, and beginning of my strength, The abundance of exaltation, And the abundance of strength;
49.4: Unstable as water, you are not abundant; For you have gone up your father's bed; Then you have polluted: My couch he went up!
49.5: Simeon and Levi are brethren! Instruments of violence--their espousals!
49.6: Into their secret, come not, O my soul! To their assembly be not united, O my honour; For in their anger they slew a man, And in their self-will eradicated a prince.
49.7: Cursed is their anger, for it is fierce, And their wrath, for it is sharp; I divide them in Jacob, And I scatter them in Israel.
49.8: Judah! you--your brethren praise you! Your hand is on the neck of your enemies, Sons of your father bow themselves to you.
49.9: A lion's whelp is Judah, For prey, my son, you have gone up; He has bent, he has crouched as a lion, And as a lioness; who causes him to arise?
49.10: The sceptre turns not aside from Judah, And a lawgiver from between his feet, Till his Seed come; And his is the obedience of peoples.
49.11: Binding to the vine his ass, And to the choice vine the colt of his ass, He has washed in wine his clothing, And in the blood of grapes his covering;
49.12: Red are eyes with wine, And white are teeth with milk!
49.13: Zebulun at a haven of the seas does dwell, And he is for a haven of ships; And his side is to Zidon.
49.14: Issacher is a strong ass, Crouching between the two folds;
49.15: And he sees rest that it is good, And the land that it is pleasant, And he inclines his shoulder to bear, And is to tribute a servant.
49.16: Dan does judge his people, As one of the tribes of Israel;
49.17: Dan is a serpent by the way, An adder by the path, Which is biting the horse's heels, And its rider falls backward.
49.18: For Your salvation I have waited, Jehovah!
49.19: Gad! a troop assaults him, But he assaults last.
49.20: Out of Asher his bread is fat; And he gives dainties of a king.
49.21: Naphtali is a hind sent away, Who is giving beauteous young ones.
49.22: Joseph is a fruitful son; A fruitful son by a fountain, Daughters step over the wall;
49.23: And embitter him--yes, they have striven, Yes, hate him do archers;
49.24: And his bow abides in strength, And strengthened are the arms of his hands By the hands of the Mighty One of Jacob, From where is a shepherd, a son of Israel.
49.25: By the God of your father who helps you, And the Mighty One who blesses you, Blessings of the heavens from above, Blessings of the deep lying under, Blessings of breasts and womb; --
49.26: Your father's blessings have been mighty Above the blessings of my progenitors, To the limit of the heights age-during They are for the head of Joseph, And for the crown of the one Separate from his brethren.
49.27: Benjamin! a wolf tears; In the morning he eats prey, And at evening he apportions spoil.'
49.28: All these are the twelve tribes of Israel, and this is that which their father has spoken to them, and he blesses them; each according to his blessing he has blessed them.
49.29: And he commands them, and says to them, `I am being gathered to my people; bury me by my fathers, at the cave which is in the field of Ephron the Hittite;
49.30: in the cave which is in the field of Machpelah, which is on the front of Mamre, in the land of Canaan, which Abraham bought with the field from Ephron the Hittite for a possession of a burying-place;
49.31: (there they buried Abraham and Sarah his wife; there they buried Isaac and Rebekah his wife; and there I buried Leah);
49.32: the purchase of the field and of the cave which is in it, is from Sons of Heth.'
49.33: And Jacob finishes commanding his sons, and gathers up his feet to the bed, and expires, and is gathered to his people.

50.1: And Joseph falls on his father's face, and weeps over him, and kisses him;
50.2: and Joseph commands his servants, the physicians, to embalm his father, and the physicians embalm Israel;
50.3: and they fulfil for him forty days, for so they fulfil the days of the embalmed, and the Egyptians weep for him seventy days.
50.4: And the days of his weeping pass away, and Joseph speaks to the house of Pharaoh, saying, `If, I pray you, I have found grace in your eyes, speak, I pray you, in the ears of Pharaoh, saying,
50.5: My father caused me to swear, saying, Indeed, I am dying; in my burying-place which I have prepared for myself in the land of Canaan, there do you bury me; and now, let me go up, I pray you, and bury my father, and return;'
50.6: and Pharaoh says, `Go up and bury your father, as he caused you to swear.'
50.7: And Joseph goes up to bury his father, and go up with him do all the servants of Pharaoh, elders of his house, and all the elders of the land of Egypt,
50.8: and all the house of Joseph, and his brethren, and the house of his father; only their infants, and their flock, and their herd, have they left in the land of Goshen;
50.9: and there go up with him both chariot and horsemen, and the camp is very great.
50.10: And they come to the threshing-floor of Atad, which is beyond the Jordan, and they lament there, a lamentation great and very grievous; and he makes for his father a mourning seven days,
50.11: and the inhabitant of the land, the Canaanite, see the mourning in the threshing-floor of Atad, and say, `A grievous mourning is this to the Egyptians;' therefore has one called its name `The mourning of the Egyptians,' which is beyond the Jordan.
50.12: And his sons do to him so as he commanded them,
50.13: and his sons bear him away to the land of Canaan, and bury him in the cave of the field of Machpelah, which Abraham bought with the field for a possession of a burying-place, from Ephron the Hittite, on the front of Mamre.
50.14: And Joseph turns back to Egypt, he and his brethren, and all who are going up with him to bury his father, after his burying his father.
50.15: And the brethren of Joseph see that their father is dead, and say, `Perhaps Joseph does hate us, and does certainly return to us all the evil which we did with him.'
50.16: And they give a charge for Joseph, saying, `Your father commanded before his death, saying,
50.17: Thus you do say to Joseph, I pray you, bear, I pray you, with the transgression of your brethren, and their sin, for they have done you evil; and now, bear, we pray you, with the transgression of the servants of the God of your father;' and Joseph weeps in their speaking to him.
50.18: And his brethren also go and fall before him, and say, `Indeed, we are to you for servants.'
50.19: And Joseph says to them, `Fear not, for am I in the place of God?
50.20: As for you, you devised against me evil--God devised it for good, in order to do as at this day, to keep alive a numerous people;
50.21: and now, fear not: I do nourish you and your infants;' and he comforts them, and speaks to their heart.
50.22: And Joseph dwells in Egypt, he and the house of his father, and Joseph lives a hundred and ten years,
50.23: and Joseph looks on Ephraim's sons of the third generation; sons also of Machir, son of Manasseh, have been born on the knees of Joseph.
50.24: And Joseph says to his brethren, `I am dying, and God does certainly inspect you, and has caused you to go up from this land, to the land which He has sworn to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.'
50.25: And Joseph causes the sons of Israel to swear, saying, `God does certainly inspect you, and you have brought up my bones from this place.'
50.26: And Joseph dies, a son of an hundred and ten years, and they embalm him, and he is put into a coffin in Egypt.
